But as matters progressed and that disinterest led to her being completely indifferent to the fact that I couldn't even get the basics I needed to keep the kennels and mews running from the palace treasury..." Yes, you can see how that might be a problem. And still he stayed on despite everything crumbling all about him? "I sent off my apprentices — things were already bad in the palace, but with the demoness' arrival they were steadily getting worse by the day. And as to why I didn't leave myself... I guess something of the oath I took to the old king and queen still stuck with me to the bitter end. Not that it mattered." He looses a bitter laugh. "Not when Alissa sent me on a wild goose chase after her sister and took the opportunity when I was gone to strip the kennels and mews of everything remotely valuable and sell it off. What a fool I was, to give my loyalty to her, and yet I did." | I know it may sound wrong of me to say it, but when I think back on it the demoness arriving in the palace and corrupting everyone may have been a good thing," Elyon muses. "I know this opinion may be unpopular, but I still feel it needs to be said." Well then, he can explain his reasoning, and you'll hear him out. "Sure, the demoness was bad, I think we can all agree on that. But even without her, the way Alissa was going about things was just as destructive, if slower. And a painful, long decline over years is arguably even worse that everything that happened, because it was much, much easier to cover up. It was much, much easier to not notice the slow slide into rot; I only realized it when I compared my budget for the kennels and mews over the years and found it'd been steadily shrinking. The treasury was being drained all the same, the wine cellars were just as empty, Alissa's courtiers just as rotten. The demoness' arrival just accelerated the festering and made the changes so quick that people who weren't wilfully blind had to start noticing." Elthara, for that matter... "She was one of the first, and one whom Alissa couldn't just dismiss from the palace without inconvenient questions being asked. But back to the point, things got so bad so quickly that the then-dutchess of the rim had to go and get help. If it wasn't for the demoness, Alissa's reign would have dragged on for decades more, and the decline would have proceeded at such an appropriately yet inexorably glacial pace that everyone would have just accepted it as being normal. By arriving and bringing things to a head, she allowed the scab to be finally ripped off and the wound to be allowed to heal. I know it sounds cruel of me to say that, champion, but what happened may have been for the better in the long run. "Or it may just be me trying to whitewash my complicity and cowardice in all this by staying silent in this whole matter," Elyon admits with a bitter laugh. "Judge me if you will, champion, but that's all I have to say." |" You do have to ask... how exactly did Kasyrra worm her way into the confidence of the court at large? Certainly she didn't appear as a demoness outright when she first arrived at the palace, did she? Elyon scratches his stubbled chin and thinks on the matter. "I can't say I was invited to any of the parties Alissa threw — not as a guest, anyway, and even if I were I don't think I could've stood it. Can't say I rightly have the full picture of what was going on." That's all right, you don't think anyone save for Kasyrra and maybe Alissa herself understood the entirety of what was happening. At the same time, that's how you piece together the whole picture, from fragments of other peoples' perspectives. So, if he wouldn't mind telling you? "Well, I'll tell you what I know. At the beginning, word got out amongst the palace staff that the Queen had found a new friend in one of her party guests — a pretty face who knew how to liven things up quite well. Given how much Alissa hated ennui, it only made sense that she'd take well to such a personality; the only question was that no one could quite tell who this lady was, how she'd managed to get herself invited to the party, or where she'd come from. It was, as they say, quite the mystery." Didn't that raise suspicion? Something as blatantly obvious as this should've raised alarm bells in anyone sensible. "Amongst us common folk, it did. Some of us, anyway. Elthara was certainly disapproving, but then she disapproved of anything and everything Alissa was doing at that stage, so it wasn't out of the ordinary in the slightest. The court just saw it all as a great mystery and game — whatever happened to the court of Atheldred's time I don't know, but it damn well wasn't this one. No sense of danger and urgency, and Alissa's attitude didn't help. And as for us little people... who cares what we have to say? Certainly not anyone who could conceivably do anything about it. What was I going to do, challenge Alissa for the crown in single combat? I suppose it was a small mercy that neither she nor the demoness took a personal interest in me, for what it was worth. "Nevertheless, the queen's new bosom friend was the talk of the palace staff. Some of the maids claimed that she was a half-sexed with a massive prick swinging under those skirts, but others said she was too well-built for that. I heard Elthara tried to discreetly inquire into this newcomer's background, but came hard up against a brick wall. The woman had absolutely no history, no background, no family or trail or home district of the Winter City. It was as if she'd appeared out of thin air." And that's exactly what Kasyrra did. Popped into existence out of a portal. Elyon just shakes his head at that. "Gods. I tried to help Elthara, track this new confidante's comings and goings with the hounds, but answers were few and those we did get raised more questions than they closed. Eventually, by the time the then-dutchess ran away from the palace for good and I was ordered into the woods after her, Elthara said she was going to confront Alissa with all the evidence she'd gathered." And that's presumably how she ended up on her own altar with a giant dildo shoved up her butt. Elyon just sighs. "And so in a way, we both suffered the same fate, although the mark it left on me is more visible than hers." ] "

rows.original: [rand |There hasn't been much call for hunts lately, have there? "No, no, none of that. Not just because there aren't the animals or the money for such luxuries after everything that's happened, but also because there's no one around to participate in them, either. A hunt is as much a social gathering as it is sport, a chance for the nobs to rub shoulders and talk a bit, and well, there aren't many of them around these days, are there? Not until [etheryn.crowned |her Majesty |the regent ] makes a bunch more, I guess, but that's still a long ways off yet. "I'm trying to be optimistic about it all — I still haven't lost what my predecessors accumulated over the centuries, and maybe I can still find my old apprentices out there in the city, ask the both of them to come back. Almost all the animals are gone... but the druids' wargs do present opportunities to start new lines, get some fresh blood into this animal husbandry business. I'm not sure if I'm still capable of doing a wild take of a bird at my age, but it'll be interesting to see if I've still not it. If not, that's what apprentices are for." You see. "I'm not going to lie, champion. There isn't going to be another actual hunt in my lifetime, not with the ruin that's been wrought upon the palace of ice. But at the very least, I owe it to [etheryn.crowned |her Majesty |the regent ] to at least make sure that her grandchildren, if not hopefully her children, will be able to indulge in the simple joys of the hunt — plant trees whose shade you will never sit under and all that." |"Elthara's got me workin the books most of these days," Elyon laments with a small sigh. "I don't understand economics, taxation and all that, but I can make numbers add up. It's not much, but apparently it's all we have, and if I can take some of that weight off Elthara's shoulders I guess I'm obliged to. It's not as if the kennels and mews are taking up anything of my time like they used to, so I can be out here in the ballroom gardens when I'd be tending to the animals in the king dowager's time." As far as people from the previous administration who actually know something about stewardship of a city-state go, he's amongst the most qualified for the task. "Only because everyone else who could do the job better has been removed from the palace," comes the dry retort. "But you're right, champion — we do what we must. After all, before all this happened, Elthara was merely high priestess and her influence only stretched to the theological. She may have had the responsibility of managing the Festivus balls, but certainly didn't control the treasury's pursestrings the way she does now. The woman's certainly coming up in life — if you didn't know any better, it could be mistaken for a power grab. Ha!" But he's adjusting well to his new responsibilities? "What's the point of this, champion?" ...Whatever does he mean? "I mean, what's the point of flapping your lips at me asking questions you know the answers to? If it isn't going well for me, what do you expect me to do about it? Say no to Elthara? Leave the palace? Drink myself to death on what's left on the remainder of the wine cellar? No, I'm just going to do what I swore to the old queen to do and put my nose to the grindstone for the var Ridells until there's blood all over the floor. Whether I like staring at the books all day is immaterial, whether an old dog like me can learn new tricks doesn't matter. It's got to get done anyway. "I get it. You want to be nice, be friends, work together for [etheryn.crowned |her Majesty |the regent ]. I can dig that, fine. Maybe you could even offer some small luxury from beyond the city if I was feeling down. But that doesn't change the fact that when it comes down to it, there's absolutely nothing that we can do because there isn't anything to spare for luxuries and any single one of us abdicating our responsibilities would be disastrous. And you bringing this up, well-meaning or not, drives home our powerlessness at it all. Yes, it's a shitty situation. Yes, we've got to work through it all whether we like it or not. But could you please not remind us of the absolute sorry state everything is in, even if you're presumably trying to be nice? It's just doing the exact opposite!" Demonic eyes wide, teeth gritted, Elyon clenches and unclenches his fists several times, then exhales all of a sudden in a long sigh. "I'm going to leave now. This is too disheartening." |"When you're not dragging her off to heed the call of adventure, [etheryn.crowned |her Majesty |the regent ] often comes down to the mews for advice on Harrick. The bird may be one of the few joys she has left in this world... not that she had many to begin with. As someone who has sworn service to her line, I'm obligated to tend to her bird to the best of my ability, even if she's come a long way since she first showed interest in falconry. "It is, at least, a small part of the job that I was once trained to do. A fragment of a memory that harkens back to better times, when her father was alive." What else has he been doing these days to try and restore the kennels and mews? "The druids, mostly. They're loathe to give up anything they have, but I think I may be able to convince them to donate a pup or two as a show of goodwill towards the eventual reunification of our peoples." What does he think of that? "I don't. That's diplomacy, and I'm no diplomat. What I do want to get my ugly hands on are their animals. If I could just get them to let one of their specimens stud for the handful of bitches remaining with the royal guard..." Tsk, he's really into it, isn't he? A thin-lipped smile. "If you did any animal husbandry, my dear Champion of Winter, you'd start seeing things this way, too. I'm just trying to keep an optimistic view of things — having everything burnt to the ground just means that you've the chance to build up something completely new and better instead, right? Oh, it could be much worse, yes. But it also could be much better!" With that tone of voice, you can't tell if he's being genuine or just sardonic... "Oh, I'm quite serious about this, even if I know I'm just going to get the stone rolling and will never see where it ends up. That, and the alternative is to be faced with crushing, paralyzing despair at the loss of generations upon generations of work by the huntsmasters who came before me. So yes, if I'm going to be getting more hawks and hounds to replace what was lost, I might as well start with quality and work my way from there. The lady of light herself couldn't have sent the druids crawling back to us at a better time." |"It feels... strange, for lack of a better word," Elyon muses when you ask the question. "I remember a time when the entire palace was bustling with people, and now that things with this whole demoness matter have been settled, people are starting to trickle back. Good help is still hard to get, though, which is why Elthara's still doing the jobs of three, four people when it comes down to it. I don't doubt that once some kind of stability returns to the palace, [etheryn.crowned |her Majesty |the regent ] will be promoting people to fill the jobs the old guard weren't after all. If the kennels and mews are getting some fresh blood from all this, there's no reason why the upper crust of the Winter City can't." Why, is he angling to become a nob himself? Then maybe he'll be the one actually participating in a hunt instead of just being on the sidelines. "Ha! That's not for me. Eternally striving from dawn to dusk, trying to garner more influence while at the same time terrified of losing what you have — every time I saw any of Alissa's hangers-on, they all gave the impression of having to run very quickly to remain in the same spot, if you get what I mean. This sort of nonsense is no way to live, I'd tire of that kind of bullshit in no time. Plus, I've got that bailiff continually breathing down my neck, just waiting for me to slip up so she can take my head from my shoulders. If I tried to angle myself to rise any further, she'd just interpret that as me trying to grab power. "No, we need people who can actually do useful things, and I'm happy to say that given the current circumstances in the palace, all the feckless idiots, lazy stayabouts, and useless eaters are going to be staying away until the time of [etheryn.crowned |her Majesty |the regent ]'s grandchildren at least. I just hope we get a little more time out of this do-over." |"There hasn't been much spare time for it, but I've been going over everything that wasn't trashed or sold and building a copy of it by hand, putting words to paper. The sleds and boar spears, the horns and gloves... everything." Why, though? By his own admission, being able to go on hunts is a luxury, one that the palace can ill-afford at this point. "So that it doesn't get lost, fool!" Elyon snaps. "How to build a proper hunting dogsled may seem trivial to you — to so many other people — but if this whole business with Alissa and the demoness has taught me anything, it's how easily these things are lost. My predecessors may have been content with handing everything down by word of mouth for fear of our trade secrets being stolen, but I've come to realize the risk of their loss outweighs any such concerns at this point. Ever since I returned to the palace, I've done more writing than I used to for the first half of my life. "Even if something does happen to me, even if I don't manage to make it, even if that bailiff gets her wish and removes my head from my shoulders, at least what I know won't be lost and anyone who comes after me will be able to pick up the things I've left behind. It's... it's all I can hope for, champion. When I was living it, the decline felt so slow that I couldn't be bothered... and now when I look back on it the whole matter feels like it all went by in the blink of an eye." So, a museum of sorts. "If that's what you want to call it, champion. I don't see any of these getting any real use anytime soon, given the state of the palace, but at least there'll not just be the instructions for fashioning a proper falconry glove or hunting dogsled, but also an example of what one should look like. And that..." he sighs. "That requires that I make them to be as flawless as possible. I may have never tried so hard to be perfect in my life before, champion. Which I suppose goes to show how lax I've been all this while... "But I suppose it means I have hope that everything will get better now that Alissa and her demoness are gone, champion. Hope that maybe things will get better to the point where the var Ridells can hold hunts again. Then, whoever who's the master of hawks and hounds in that time will have studied both the writings and implements I've left behind, even if something happens to me before I can adequately pass on what I know in person. Maybe it's a false hope, but I don't believe it is. I really don't." ]
rows.translation: [rand |最近似乎没什么人愿意参加狩猎活动了，对吧？ “不，并不是这个原因。不仅仅是因为发生了那些事情之后，已经没有足够的动物可供狩猎，也没有钱来享受这样的奢侈活动了；更重要的原因是，根本没有人愿意参加这些狩猎活动。狩猎其实既是一种运动，也是一种社交活动——那些贵族们可以通过狩猎来结识彼此、聊聊天。不过这些天，这样的贵族已经不多了吧？至少现在是这样。 [etheryn.crowned |女王陛下 |摄政王 ] 我想，这样还能做出更多成果，但距离真正实现目标还有很长的路要走。 “我尽量保持乐观的态度——毕竟我还没有失去前人几个世纪以来积累下来的东西，或许我还能在城里找到我的那些老学徒，邀请他们俩回来。 几乎所有的动物都消失了……但是德鲁伊们的狼人确实为重新开始这项畜牧业提供了机会，也让这个行业注入了新的活力。我不确定自己在这个年纪是否还能像以前那样熟练地捕捉野鸟，不过看看自己是否还能保持这种能力，倒也挺有意思的。 否则，学徒的存在意义就在于此。” “你明白的。” “说实话，冠军。在我的有生之年内，不会再有真正的狩猎机会了。毕竟冰之宫殿已经遭受了如此严重的破坏。 但至少，我欠这个 [etheryn.crowned |女王陛下 |摄政王 ] 至少要确保她的孙子孙女们，甚至希望她的孩子们，能够享受到狩猎带来的简单乐趣——比如种植那些永远无法在树荫下乘凉的树木，以及做诸如此类的事情。 |这些天，埃尔萨拉总是让我忙于处理各种账目，”伊利恩轻叹道，“我并不懂经济学、税收之类的知识，但我至少能确保那些数字是正确的。虽然这不算什么，但显然这是我们目前能做的全部事情了。如果我能帮埃尔萨拉分担一些负担，我想我也有责任这么做。毕竟现在，照顾那些动物已经不像过去那样占用我太多时间了，所以现在我可以在舞厅花园里休息，而过去这些时间都是用来照顾王太后的宠物的。 就那些在管理城邦方面确实具备相关经验的前任政府成员而言，他是最适合担任这一职务的人选之一。 “只是因为所有那些能够把这项工作做得更好的人都已经被赶出了宫廷罢了，”有人冷冷地回应道。 但你说得对，冠军——我们只是在做自己该做的事。毕竟，在这一切发生之前，艾尔塔拉只不过是一位大祭司，她的影响力也仅限于宗教领域。她或许负责管理节日庆典的相关事务，但绝对没有像现在这样掌握财政大权。 这个女人确实正在事业上取得成功——要是你不太了解内情的话，还可能会误以为她在试图攫取权力呢。哈！ 但他正在很好地适应这些新的职责吧？ “这样做有什么意义呢，冠军？” ……他到底想表达什么意思呢？ “我的意思是，既然你知道那些问题的答案，那为什么还要问我这些问题呢？ 如果我的事情进展不顺利，你还能指望我怎么做呢？拒绝埃尔萨拉的邀请吗？离开宫殿吗？或者把酒窖里剩下的酒都喝轻型然后自杀吗？不，我只会做我曾经向那位老女王许下的承诺：为拉里德尔家族拼命工作，直到把整个地面都弄得血迹斑斑为止。 不管我是否 喜欢 整天埋头读书也没用，像我这样的老狗能不能学会新本领也不重要。反正这件事必须得完成。 “我明白了。你是想表现得友善一些，想和我们成为朋友，想一起合作 [etheryn.crowned |女王陛下 |摄政王 ]我挺赞同这个想法的，没问题。如果我心情不好的话，你们甚至可以提供一些来自城市以外的小礼物来安慰我。但事实依然是，归根结底，关键还是 我们根本无能为力。 因为我们根本没有多余的资源来享受奢华，而如果我们中的任何一个人放弃了自己的责任，后果将会非常严重。而你提出这个问题，无论你的出发点是好的还是坏，都让我们更加清楚地意识到了自己的无力感。没错，这确实是一个糟糕的局面。 是的，无论我们是否愿意，我们都必须解决这一切问题。但是，能不能请不要再提醒我们目前的情况有多糟糕了呢？尽管你可能是出于好意，但这样做反而适得其反！埃利恩双眼圆睁，牙关紧咬，反复握紧又松开双拳，最终长长地叹了口气。 “我现在就要离开。这里太令人沮丧了。" |当你没有带着她去追寻冒险的召唤时， [etheryn.crowned |女王陛下 |摄政王 ] 她经常去那些小巷里向别人请教关于哈里克的事。这只鸟可能是她在这个世界上为数不多的乐趣之一了……其实她本来就没什么乐趣可言。作为对她家族效忠的人，我有责任尽我所能照顾好她的这只鸟，即使自从她第一次对猎鹰术产生兴趣以来，她已经发生了很大的变化。 这至少是我曾经被训练来做的那份工作的一小部分。它是那些回忆中的一片段，那些回忆让人回想起那些更美好的时轻型——当时她的父亲还活着。” 那么，这些天来，他还做了些什么来努力修复那些狗舍和马厩呢？ 主要是那些德鲁伊。他们非常不愿意放弃自己拥有的任何东西，但我想我或许能够说服他们捐赠一两只幼崽，以此表达对我们两国人民最终重逢的善意。” 他对此有什么看法呢？ 我不感兴趣。那属于外交手部段，而我可不是什么外交家。我真正想要得到的，是他们那些动物。要是我能让他们把其中一只标本让给皇家卫队里剩下的那些女人……” 啧，他还真挺热衷于这个的，不是吗？ 她露出一个淡淡的微笑：“亲爱的冬之冠军，如果你也从事过畜牧业，你就会明白我的想法。我只是在努力保持乐观的态度——毕竟一切被烧毁，恰恰意味着你有机会重建一些全新的、更好的东西，不是吗？当然，情况也可能更糟……但同时也有可能变得更好！ 从他那样的肌肉度来看，根本无法分辨他是认真的还是在挖苦别人…… “哦，我是真的挺认真的，虽然我也知道，这样做只会引发一连串的反应，而且永远也不会知道最终会是什么结果。 否则，我就不得不面对这样一种令人崩溃、令人绝望的现实：我之前的那些猎场主管们耗费了数代人的努力，而这些成果最终却全部白费了。所以，如果我真的想要引进更多的鹰和猎犬来弥补这些损失，那么我最好从选择质量上乘的猎犬开始，然后再逐步扩大规模。 就连那位轻型之女神本人，也不可能选择在一个更恰当的时刻，让那些德鲁伊们重新回到我们身边。 |用一个不太恰当的词来说，这种感觉……确实很奇怪，”当你提出这个问题时，埃利昂这样说道。“我还记得曾经有一段时间，整个宫殿里到处都是人，而如今，随着那个女恶魔的事情终于得到了解决，人们才开始陆续回来。不过，好帮手部仍然很难找到，因此实际上埃尔萨拉现在要承担三到四个人的工作量。我毫不怀疑，一旦宫殿重新恢复了稳定，情况一定会好转的。 [etheryn.crowned |女王陛下 |摄政王 ] 这其实是在招募新人来填补那些老派人士不愿意担任的职位。如果这些新成员能为各个机构注入新鲜血液，那么冬城的上层社会也完全没有理由不能这样做。 难道，他是想自己也成为贵族吗？ 那么，也许最终真正参与狩猎的会是他，而而不只是站在一旁观战。 “哈！那不适合我。从早到晚不停地奋斗，试图获得更多的权力，同时又害怕失去已经拥有的东西——每次我看到艾莉莎那些跟班们，他们给人的感觉都是：必须拼命努力才能保持现有的地位，你懂我的意思吧。 这种荒谬的生活方式根本无法让人正常生活，我很快就会对这种无聊的事情感到厌烦。更何况，还有那个执达员一直盯着我，就等着我犯错，这样她就可以把我“除掉”了。 如果我试图采取某种手部段来进一步升迁，她只会认为我在试图攫取权力。 “不，我们需要的是那些真正有能力的人。 做 这些有用的东西……我很高兴地说，鉴于目前宫中的状况，所有那些无能的蠢货、懒惰的人以及只会吃不会干活的人，都会被赶走，直到……那个时候为止。 [etheryn.crowned |女王陛下 |摄政王 ]至少还有孙子孙女们。我只希望我们能从这次重新开始中得到多一点的时间。 |其实并没有太多空闲时间来做这件事，但我把所有没有被丢弃或卖掉的东西都重新整理出来，然后亲手部一一复制，把那些细节都记录下来——雪橇、野猪矛、角和手部套……所有这些东西。” 但为什么呢？按照他自己的说法，能够去打猎其实是一种奢侈，而目前宫廷根本负担不起这种奢侈。 别让它丢了，笨蛋！”伊莱恩厉声说道，“建造一辆合适的猎犬雪橇对你来说——对很多人来说——可能看起来是一件很简单的事情，但通过与艾丽莎以及那个女恶魔的这些经历，我终于明白了：这些东西其实是多么容易丢失的。 我的前任们可能因为担心我们的商业秘密会被泄露，所以选择通过口口相传的方式来传递所有信息，但我现在意识到，这些秘密丢失所带来的风险，远远超过了他们当初的顾虑。自从我回到宫廷之后，我写的文件数量比人生前半段的时间里写的还要多。 即使我遭遇了什么，即使我无法成功完成这件事，即使那个执达员得逞，将我的头从脖子上砍下来，至少我所知道的一切不会消失，我的后人能够继承我留下的东西。这就是我唯一的希望了，冠军。当初我亲身经历这些的时候，那种衰败的过程显得如此缓慢，以至于我根本没有在意……而现在回想起来，这一切仿佛都在一瞬间发生了。 所以，可以说是一种博物馆吧。 “如果你想这么称呼它的话，冠军。考虑到宫殿目前的状况，我觉得这些东西在短期内根本不会被用到，但至少这里不仅会提供制作合格的猎鹰手部套或猎犬雪橇所需的说明，还会展示实际成品。 应该 看起来是这样……而且那个……”他叹了口气，“这意味着我必须把它们做得尽可能完美。我想我这辈子可能从未这么努力过，想要做到完美无缺，冠军。这也说明，一直以来我的要求其实都太宽松了。但我想，这意味着现在艾莉莎和她的恶魔女仆已经离开了，一切都有希望变得更好了，冠军。也许情况会好转到里德尔一家能够再次组织狩猎活动的地步。 那么，在那个时代，凡是能够驾驭鹰隼与猎犬的人，必定会研读我留下的这些文字与工具。即使我在有幸亲自传授这些知识之前就离世了，也一定会有其他人继承我的事业。或许这只是一个渺茫的希望，但我并不这么认为。 我真的不知道。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |There hasn't been much call for hunts lately, have there? "No, no, none of that. Not just because there aren't the animals or the money for such luxuries after everything that's happened, but also because there's no one around to participate in them, either. A hunt is as much a social gathering as it is sport, a chance for the nobs to rub shoulders and talk a bit, and well, there aren't many of them around these days, are there? Not until [etheryn.crowned |her Majesty |the regent ] makes a bunch more, I guess, but that's still a long ways off yet. "I'm trying to be optimistic about it all — I still haven't lost what my predecessors accumulated over the centuries, and maybe I can still find my old apprentices out there in the city, ask the both of them to come back. Almost all the animals are gone... but the druids' wargs do present opportunities to start new lines, get some fresh blood into this animal husbandry business. I'm not sure if I'm still capable of doing a wild take of a bird at my age, but it'll be interesting to see if I've still not it. If not, that's what apprentices are for." You see. "I'm not going to lie, champion. There isn't going to be another actual hunt in my lifetime, not with the ruin that's been wrought upon the palace of ice. But at the very least, I owe it to [etheryn.crowned |her Majesty |the regent ] to at least make sure that her grandchildren, if not hopefully her children, will be able to indulge in the simple joys of the hunt — plant trees whose shade you will never sit under and all that." |"Elthara's got me workin the books most of these days," Elyon laments with a small sigh. "I don't understand economics, taxation and all that, but I can make numbers add up. It's not much, but apparently it's all we have, and if I can take some of that weight off Elthara's shoulders I guess I'm obliged to. It's not as if the kennels and mews are taking up anything of my time like they used to, so I can be out here in the ballroom gardens when I'd be tending to the animals in the king dowager's time." As far as people from the previous administration who actually know something about stewardship of a city-state go, he's amongst the most qualified for the task. "Only because everyone else who could do the job better has been removed from the palace," comes the dry retort. "But you're right, champion — we do what we must. After all, before all this happened, Elthara was merely high priestess and her influence only stretched to the theological. She may have had the responsibility of managing the Festivus balls, but certainly didn't control the treasury's pursestrings the way she does now. The woman's certainly coming up in life — if you didn't know any better, it could be mistaken for a power grab. Ha!" But he's adjusting well to his new responsibilities? "What's the point of this, champion?" ...Whatever does he mean? "I mean, what's the point of flapping your lips at me asking questions you know the answers to? If it isn't going well for me, what do you expect me to do about it? Say no to Elthara? Leave the palace? Drink myself to death on what's left on the remainder of the wine cellar? No, I'm just going to do what I swore to the old queen to do and put my nose to the grindstone for the var Ridells until there's blood all over the floor. Whether I like staring at the books all day is immaterial, whether an old dog like me can learn new tricks doesn't matter. It's got to get done anyway. "I get it. You want to be nice, be friends, work together for [etheryn.crowned |her Majesty |the regent ]. I can dig that, fine. Maybe you could even offer some small luxury from beyond the city if I was feeling down. But that doesn't change the fact that when it comes down to it, there's absolutely nothing that we can do because there isn't anything to spare for luxuries and any single one of us abdicating our responsibilities would be disastrous. And you bringing this up, well-meaning or not, drives home our powerlessness at it all. Yes, it's a shitty situation. Yes, we've got to work through it all whether we like it or not. But could you please not remind us of the absolute sorry state everything is in, even if you're presumably trying to be nice? It's just doing the exact opposite!" Demonic eyes wide, teeth gritted, Elyon clenches and unclenches his fists several times, then exhales all of a sudden in a long sigh. "I'm going to leave now. This is too disheartening." |"When you're not dragging her off to heed the call of adventure, [etheryn.crowned |her Majesty |the regent ] often comes down to the mews for advice on Harrick. The bird may be one of the few joys she has left in this world... not that she had many to begin with. As someone who has sworn service to her line, I'm obligated to tend to her bird to the best of my ability, even if she's come a long way since she first showed interest in falconry. "It is, at least, a small part of the job that I was once trained to do. A fragment of a memory that harkens back to better times, when her father was alive." What else has he been doing these days to try and restore the kennels and mews? "The druids, mostly. They're loathe to give up anything they have, but I think I may be able to convince them to donate a pup or two as a show of goodwill towards the eventual reunification of our peoples." What does he think of that? "I don't. That's diplomacy, and I'm no diplomat. What I do want to get my ugly hands on are their animals. If I could just get them to let one of their specimens stud for the handful of bitches remaining with the royal guard..." Tsk, he's really into it, isn't he? A thin-lipped smile. "If you did any animal husbandry, my dear Champion of Winter, you'd start seeing things this way, too. I'm just trying to keep an optimistic view of things — having everything burnt to the ground just means that you've the chance to build up something completely new and better instead, right? Oh, it could be much worse, yes. But it also could be much better!" With that tone of voice, you can't tell if he's being genuine or just sardonic... "Oh, I'm quite serious about this, even if I know I'm just going to get the stone rolling and will never see where it ends up. That, and the alternative is to be faced with crushing, paralyzing despair at the loss of generations upon generations of work by the huntsmasters who came before me. So yes, if I'm going to be getting more hawks and hounds to replace what was lost, I might as well start with quality and work my way from there. The lady of light herself couldn't have sent the druids crawling back to us at a better time." |"It feels... strange, for lack of a better word," Elyon muses when you ask the question. "I remember a time when the entire palace was bustling with people, and now that things with this whole demoness matter have been settled, people are starting to trickle back. Good help is still hard to get, though, which is why Elthara's still doing the jobs of three, four people when it comes down to it. I don't doubt that once some kind of stability returns to the palace, [etheryn.crowned |her Majesty |the regent ] will be promoting people to fill the jobs the old guard weren't after all. If the kennels and mews are getting some fresh blood from all this, there's no reason why the upper crust of the Winter City can't." Why, is he angling to become a nob himself? Then maybe he'll be the one actually participating in a hunt instead of just being on the sidelines. "Ha! That's not for me. Eternally striving from dawn to dusk, trying to garner more influence while at the same time terrified of losing what you have — every time I saw any of Alissa's hangers-on, they all gave the impression of having to run very quickly to remain in the same spot, if you get what I mean. This sort of nonsense is no way to live, I'd tire of that kind of bullshit in no time. Plus, I've got that bailiff continually breathing down my neck, just waiting for me to slip up so she can take my head from my shoulders. If I tried to angle myself to rise any further, she'd just interpret that as me trying to grab power. "No, we need people who can actually do useful things, and I'm happy to say that given the current circumstances in the palace, all the feckless idiots, lazy stayabouts, and useless eaters are going to be staying away until the time of [etheryn.crowned |her Majesty |the regent ]'s grandchildren at least. I just hope we get a little more time out of this do-over." |"There hasn't been much spare time for it, but I've been going over everything that wasn't trashed or sold and building a copy of it by hand, putting words to paper. The sleds and boar spears, the horns and gloves... everything." Why, though? By his own admission, being able to go on hunts is a luxury, one that the palace can ill-afford at this point. "So that it doesn't get lost, fool!" Elyon snaps. "How to build a proper hunting dogsled may seem trivial to you — to so many other people — but if this whole business with Alissa and the demoness has taught me anything, it's how easily these things are lost. My predecessors may have been content with handing everything down by word of mouth for fear of our trade secrets being stolen, but I've come to realize the risk of their loss outweighs any such concerns at this point. Ever since I returned to the palace, I've done more writing than I used to for the first half of my life. "Even if something does happen to me, even if I don't manage to make it, even if that bailiff gets her wish and removes my head from my shoulders, at least what I know won't be lost and anyone who comes after me will be able to pick up the things I've left behind. It's... it's all I can hope for, champion. When I was living it, the decline felt so slow that I couldn't be bothered... and now when I look back on it the whole matter feels like it all went by in the blink of an eye." So, a museum of sorts. "If that's what you want to call it, champion. I don't see any of these getting any real use anytime soon, given the state of the palace, but at least there'll not just be the instructions for fashioning a proper falconry glove or hunting dogsled, but also an example of what one should look like. And that..." he sighs. "That requires that I make them to be as flawless as possible. I may have never tried so hard to be perfect in my life before, champion. Which I suppose goes to show how lax I've been all this while... "But I suppose it means I have hope that everything will get better now that Alissa and her demoness are gone, champion. Hope that maybe things will get better to the point where the var Ridells can hold hunts again. Then, whoever who's the master of hawks and hounds in that time will have studied both the writings and implements I've left behind, even if something happens to me before I can adequately pass on what I know in person. Maybe it's a false hope, but I don't believe it is. I really don't." ] "

Looking askance, Ryn twiddles her fingers. "He blames himself for my father's death." If she knows why and she's clearly more than willing, then why hasn't she forgiven him for it? "Because he wouldn't a-accept it either, [pc.name]. That's the problem. He was leading the hunt on the day my father died, he was the one who checked over the boar spear my father was u-using. rows.translation: 当你正准备踏入那座冰之宫殿宏伟的入口大厅时， [party.has etheryn |注意，瑞恩落在你后面有些距离了，她的脚步变得缓慢，看起来似乎在沉思着什么。 “怎么了？是在思考什么重要的事情吗？” “哦！呃，我只是在想 [pc.name]这件事我已经考虑了一段时间了。 |你注意到Ryn正从附近的某根柱子后面朝你张望，她努力保持低调，同时向你招手部示意过来。你不太明白为什么她要在自己家里搞得这么隐秘，但也许等你靠近一些，就会知道原因了。 “嘘！ [pc.name]在这里！ ] 现在，这一切到底是为了什么？ [etheryn.lowConfidence |瑞恩艰难地咽了口唾沫，环顾着入口处的走廊，显然是在确认周围没有其他人会偷听他们的谈话。“我，呃，听说你一直在打听关于‘鹰与猎犬之主’的事情，对吧？没错。你一直努力地对他好，按照她的要求去行事……但说实话，他并没有对你的好意给予任何回应。其中一部分原因可能是他受到了腐败的影响，但你并不认为这才是全部原因。 大多数时候他还算可以，只是偶尔会突然发脾气……他对其他人也会这样吗？ “对埃尔萨拉来说，可能有一两次吧。不过对我从来不会。” 但愿不会吧——她又不是他唯一的人啊。 [etheryn.crowned |女王 |摄政者 ]也是那个在他几乎失去机会时依然给予他机会的女人。话虽如此，还是回到正题吧——那么，这一切到底是怎么回事呢？ “我……我想我知道是什么在困扰他了……” 好吧，继续说吧。 前几天，我们聊到了在艾莉莎派他去试图救我之后，他发生了什么，然后话题就转到了他现在长成什么样子了，”瑞恩继续说道，“我提出可以用宫殿的资金带他去见一位炼金术士，看看是否能对他的那些眼睛和爪子做些什么。不过，你上次见到他的时候，他看起来还和以前一样。难道没有发生什么变化吗？ “其实，那个并不是问题所在。我们甚至都没有机会去见他——尽管我主动提出要陪他一起去，但他坚决拒绝。这可真有意思。他有没有说明原因呢？” “他说他……不配接受这份礼物。” 哦。对于他来说，能够如此慷慨地拒绝一位君主赠送的礼物，哪怕是私下赠送的……以伊利恩在宫殿里居住的时间来看，他应该很清楚，这种行为绝非轻率所能做出的。 非常 嗯……我知道原因。”瑞恩侧着头，手部指不停地转动着，“他把自己父亲去世的责任归咎于自己。” 如果她知道原因，而且显然也愿意接受这个事实，那为什么还没有原谅他呢？ “因为他自己也不愿意接受这个事实。 [pc.name]问题就在这里。我父亲去世的那天，正是他在带领狩猎队；也是他检查了我父亲使用的那支野猪矛。那支矛突然断了，愤怒的野猪趁机逼近，转眼间我父亲就被野猪刺中了。那个人现在一定很痛苦吧 [pc.name]他根本不会接受我给他的任何东西。 “但是，他可能会接受你给他的东西。” 你说什么？我不太明白你的意思。从你和伊利恩的相处来看，那个人简直是个脾气暴躁的混蛋——有一半的时间，你都会觉得他几乎无法忍受你的存在；而另外一半时间，他则表现得冷漠而刻薄。 [pc.name]他也认识E-埃尔萨拉。但他并不认识你——他不会认为你这么做是出于同情，或是觉得有义务这么做。 因为 他其实很不喜欢你，但正因为如此，你才最有机会成功。 [pc.name]你能做到我做不到的事，那就是说服他在保持自己尊严的同时接受帮助。” 她真的确定这只是出于尊严的考虑，还是其中还隐藏着其他的情绪呢？ “这重要吗？他内心其实很痛苦 嗯……我知道原因了。”瑞恩侧着头，手部指不停地转动着，这个动作与她这些天与你一起旅行后所展现出的自信截然不符。“他把自己父亲去世的责任归咎于自己。” 如果她知道原因，而且显然也愿意接受这个事实，那为什么还没有原谅他呢？ “因为他自己也不愿意接受这个事实。 [pc.name]问题就在这里。我父亲去世的那天，正是他在带领搜捕行动，也是他检查了我父亲使用的那支野猪矛。那支矛突然断了，愤怒的野猪趁机逼近，转眼间我父亲就被野猪刺中了。那个人现在一定很痛苦吧 [pc.name]他根本不会接受我给他的任何东西。 “不过，他可能会接受你给他的东西。” 你说什么？我不太明白你的意思。从你和伊利恩的相处来看，那个男人简直是个脾气暴躁的混蛋——有一半的时间，你都会觉得他几乎无法忍受你的存在；而另外一半时间，他则表现得冷漠而刻薄。 当然，你也明白，这种变化并不完全是一种自然的结果——由于他接触到了那些腐败现象，他的性格确实发生了改变，而且他也在为此而挣扎。但与此同时……这么说吧，这其实并不能成为他対待他人时采取冷漠态度的借口。 你并没有意识到，你试图帮助他的方式，其实并不比Ryn甚至埃尔萨拉所能做到的更好。 Ryn沮丧地耸了耸肩：“他了解我 [pc.name]他也认识埃尔萨拉。但他并不认识你——他不会认为你这么做是出于同情，或是觉得有义务这么做。 因为 他之所以不喜欢你，恰恰是因为你是最有成功机会的人。 [pc.name]你能做到我做不到的事，那就是说服他在保持自己尊严的同时接受帮助。” 她真的确定这只是出于尊严的考虑，还是其中还隐藏着其他的情绪呢？ “这重要吗？他内心其实很痛苦 [pc.name]我只是……我真的不想看到这样一个多年来一直如此忠实地为我的家人服务的人，即使他明知这样做并不符合自己的利益，最终还是落得这样的下场。他之所以一直支持艾丽莎以及她的统治方式，只是因为他对我的父母怀有敬意；而艾丽莎却因此背叛了他。好吧，那么她希望你对此做些什么呢？ “你能调查一下我父亲死亡的具体情况吗？” 如果她希望你这么做，你当然可以……但这样做又能有什么结果呢？ 几十年过去了，还能找到什么线索吗？应该从哪里开始搜查呢？ 莱恩摇了摇头：“如果你能发现一些我们还不知道的事情，那简直就是锦上添花。不过，目前看来……应该没有可能吧。 |就你个人而言，你觉得这完全是徒劳无功的，但如果这样做能让她安心，而且她认为这是最好的选择，那你不妨迁就她一下，只是为了证明这件事最终只会徒劳无果罢了。 |好吧，那么。无论发现新线索的可能性有多渺茫，你都要坚持沿着这条线索去调查。 ]那么，她到底想让你做什么呢？ “那时候在场的那些人，大多数现在都 消失了 多亏了艾丽莎，”瑞恩叹息道，“我知道埃尔萨拉，即使不是以大祭司的身份，也一定参与了这件事；达丽莎也同样如此。在我父亲去世后的那些日子里，有很多谣言称德鲁伊们与那起所谓的‘狩猎事故’有关。 不要去指责她什么，不过或许问问赫希娅也会有所帮助。 “等你问完之后，再回来找我。我相信，只要多打听一些，埃利恩肯定会注意到你在打探过去的事情。"

Sure, you understand that it's not wholly natural, that his personality has changed because of the corruption he was exposed to and he's struggling with it, but at the same time... that's not really an excuse to be standoffish to other people, to put it lightly. I just don't want to watch someone who's served my family so faithfully for so many years, even against h-his better judgement, end up like this. He s-stuck with Alissa and her r-rule even though he didn't agree with what she was doing because of his respect for m-my father and mother, and she betrayed him for it." All right. But no, [pc.name], what I to get across to that m-man is that we still care about him. And as for w-where you should start, maybe talking to Elthara or Daliza might help. Rumor about t-the palace for decades also claimed t-the druids were somehow involved, too, s-so maybe asking Hethia about it might be something you might want to pursue." You wouldn't put it past the druids of old to want to stain their hands with var Ridell blood, even if it was but the king dowager's. rows.original: So... this is the site where Ryn's dad died, is it? From where you're standing, the western base of the old stone bridge still stands, although its span has long since fallen into the fjord a long time ago. If you peer over the edge, you can still see the rubble of the fallen masonry, peeking out above the water... nature's reclaimed a lot of the elven ruins around here, or rather, integrated the two. It's quite tranquil, and as far as you can tell, no different from any stretch of woodland in the Frostwood. If not for the stories you've been hearing while on the wild goose chase that Ryn sent you on, you'd never have suspected its sordid past. [party.has etheryn |Looking around, Ryn swallows hard as she takes in the small first clearing and the broken bridge. She's clearly having a moment of her own, [pc.isDK |but you're sure she'll get over herself. Everyone does |but you think she needs to be alone for now; perhaps you'll be able to speak with her about the matter later. Or as it turns out, maybe that chance has just arrived ]. "So, this is where..." her voice trails off. She's never seen it before? "Well, I did pass it by when escaping from the palace on my horse, but as you can understand, I wasn't about to stop to take in the scenery." Without her around, you wouldn't have given the clearing a second glance, but now that you're here with her there's a definite melancholic air to the place. It's that kind of heart-tugging sad that really bites at one's emotions... ] Feeling that you're obligated to Ryn to at least perform a cursory search of the place, you set about giving the clearing a good look-over, taking in the oldest-looking trees for perhaps markings from — oh, you don't know. But you have to look nonetheless, right? Then it'll be easier to tell Ryn that you really tried and found nothing — [pc.bg hunter barbarian |And then your years of living in the wilderness kick in, and you whirl around, taking several purposeful steps around to an ancient pine where the shadows about one side of the broad trunk are just a shade darker than they should be. When you get within striking distance, though, Elyon steps out from around the old, rugged tree and gives you a nod. "Not bad. I didn't think I was that poorly hidden, but this dog is getting old." You chuckle dryly. He'd rather put himself down than acknowledge that you're capable of something? "Embrace the word 'and', my dear champion. It works wonders." [pc.isDK |You didn't come out all this way into the forest to take shitty sass from him, you're here to help Ryn take that stick out of his butt and start towards accepting help instead of being a little bitch about everything. |While you've tried to be understanding of his circumstances, the constant shtick of him-pushing-you-away-but-not-far-enough-so-you-can-come-back is getting quite tiring. You're trying to be patient with him for Ryn's sake, but even that has its limits. ] |And then he's at your side. Not approaching from the front, for that would be confrontational, but not from the back either, for that would be sneaking up on you. Elyon's simply approached when you... you don't even think you were preoccupied; catching his attention was the real reason you're out here in the first place, aren't you? If anyone was going to sneak up on you in these woods, it'd have to be the royal huntsman of the boreal elves, you guess... "This old dog isn't getting any younger, but I guess I should be heartened to know that I can still sneak up on the untrained." You chuckle dryly. Self-depreciating even in victory, isn't he? "It helps to have a realistic view of the situation." [pc.isDK |Well, if he doesn't mind excusing your language, fuck him and his realism |Well, that's honestly doing more harm than good, if he doesn't mind you being frank ]. You're trying to help him, Ryn's trying to help him, Elthara's trying to help him. If he wants to make it up to the var Ridell line for what he sees as his past sins, the first step on that is to get himself out of the way. That's what this whole wild goose chase has been about. ] [party.has etheryn |Elyon frowns and looks like he's about to reply with some kind of bitter comeback, but then notices Ryn standing a little ways to your side. Your elven companion gives him a pleading look and a small nod, whereupon he drops his gaze and relents. ] "Hmph. Well, I'm here. You're here. If you want us to talk, we can talk." Half-turning away from you, the huntsman sweeps his arm over the forest, the fjord, the broken bridge. "You've been asking about what happened here, champion. I know that much. So you know the story, then?" Enough to understand that he was detained as the prime suspect in the king dowager's death. "The guard wasn't wrong in that it was my fault. The only real question here is if it was murder, or a death caused through my negligience." And would he still blame himself if Hethia's suspicions were right and the druids somehow had a hand in Ryn's dad dying? "Perhaps my culpability would be lessened, that's true, but at the end of the day the fault would still lie with me. I should have checked over the boar spear to ensure it wouldn't have snapped like a twig, I should have realized that there was something with the boar and urged his Majesty to safety, regardless of whether he would heed me or not. Neither were performed to satisfaction or in time, and as such I am still to blame." "That's not to mention that whether Xadaron and her inner circle had anything to do with the king dowager's death is a question that will never be concretely answered, so this entire line of questioning is a farce. There has to be a better way for you to help me than to try and push the blame on the druids, champion." And for all that he's said, there's got to be a better way for him to live than trying to blame himself for the death of the king dowager, and by extent Alissa's rise to the throne and the collapse of the Palace of Ice into a madhouse, a fate the Winter City itself nearly shared. Does his self-imposed martyrdom actually accomplish anything here when his liege actually needs him, or is he just feeding his ego? Elyon's brow creases. "Harsh." No, that's just realistic. How does he like them apples, huh? [party.has etheryn |Ryn glances back and forth between the both of you, looking ready to leap in should the situation flare up and matters come to blows, but it hasn't come to that. Yet. After all, a var Ridell's very presence at this confrontation, by its very nature, helps cool tempers... ] Elyon grunts and shakes his head. "Have it your way, champion. If that's what you think of me." It's how he's been acting all this while. If he wants people to view him differently, maybe he should try acting differently? Look, he took the trouble of tailing you all the way out here from the palace. Why doesn't he show you around, tell you his version of things that happened that day? The huntsman gives you a long, hard look, [party.has etheryn |then turns to Etheryn and gets an encouraging nod from your elven companion in return. Maybe that was all it was going to take — Ryn pushing just a bit in the right places for him to give in — but at last Elyon gives the both of you a slow nod. "All, right. [etheryn.crowned |Your Majesty |Regent ], champion |then cocks his head and shrugs. "I don't know why [etheryn.crowned |her Majesty |the Regent ] couldn't ask me herself and had to send you on all of this, but since it's for her I'll go along with this game. Champion ], why don't you walk with me for a while and I'll show you the sights?"
rows.translation: 所以……这里就是瑞恩的父亲去世的地方吧？从你现在的位置来看，那座古老石桥的西端桥基依然矗立在那里，尽管它的桥身早已在很久以前坠入了峡湾。如果你俯身看向桥边，仍然能够看到那些坠落的石块残骸，它们隐约地露在水面上。大自然已经将这里的大部分精灵遗迹重新融入了自然环境，或者说，将它们与周围的环境融为了一体。
