rows.original: "Now, [freja.name]: how will we be making our deliveries today?" Your dragon daughter hefts a bag over her shoulder, neatly cinched so that it doesn't drag on[silly| — haha, dragon dragging on —] the ground. As soon as you arrived at the valkyrie keep and saw Eira, she insisted on helping out: et la voilà. "Super quickly!" she declares. "This is extra important stuff. It's a hero's job!" "Exactly. There's a great deal of mail and my sisters are anxious to receive it!" Eira starts moving down the way toward her first delivery even as she starts speaking. It's a speech you've heard before too, after a fashion. "Imagine if something were going wrong at home for someone in a valkyrie's family..." [freja.name]'s eyes widen for a moment, and then she bolts off to catch up with Eira. You[aileh.wintercity| and Aileh], though, settle down to watch and relax. If the goddess's messenger is ready to be the one to burn off some of your daughter's excess energy, you don't mind taking advantage of the situation. Besides, the ambience is lovely. [aileh.wintercity |Next to you, your draconic lover rests a head on your shoulder and snuggles in. "Do you think Eira's a genius?" Across the hall, you watch as the divine messenger and dragon helper emerge at breakneck speed from one side passage and rush for another. "[pc.isBimbo|Yipyup! And she's a real cutie. You're tryna get [freja.name] to be this good about chores back home — is that going okay|She might be. Any luck on getting [freja.name] to treat her other chores this way]?" She laughs. "Mixed results, dear heart. Same as before: she does everything she's supposed to. She just grumbles and goes a little bit slow." "Work is work." You smooch her on the cheek. "I still [silly|view it as an absolute|call that a] win." So, with amusement and not a small amount of awe, you watch your daughter periodically emerge into the hall, pelting after Eira as fast as she can go, using her wingies to add tiny boosts of speed and somehow avoiding the other valkyries into the bargain — although they're all agile enough to clear out of the way when your little terror comes hurtling their way. For her part, your dear heart spends most of the time relaxing right with you. Once, when [rand|Annika|Thrud|Lumia] drifts by, you three chat about things mundane and serious, but for the most part you sit with each other and enjoy the spectacle. |As you sit back and relax, the Dawn Maiden herself emerges to watch with you. "Taking a break?" You smile. "[pc.isBimbo|Uh-huh! She's got so much energy in her! It's a good thing Eira's helping out with handling it.|If Eira's willing to run some of the energy out of her...]" "And by doing work, no less," she laughs. "If only all of your little one's chores required running, hmm?" "[pc.isBimbo|Yeahhhh. She does what Mommy says, but she pouts about it too. It's kinda like me!|We've been working on that. She's good about doing everything she's supposed to. She just grumbles all the time, which... that's fair.]" You turn back to see your daughter emerge from a side passage, bag noticeably lighter, pelting hell bent for leather after Eira. "At least this is a little more fun for her." "Every time you visit, I can't help but think of what a wonderful job the three of you have done," the goddess says. "You're a good [pc.mf|father|mother], [pc.name]." "[pc.isBimbo|Thank youuuu!|Thanks.]" From across the hall, you see your daughter bounce up, letter in hand, and hand it to a smiling valkyrie. You can see the smile from across the hall, too. "[pc.isBimbo|I got super lucky with my family.|I've been lucky.]" ] You've relaxed and conversed for quite a while by the time [freja.name] bounds back your way. Her bag is lighter and her step — somehow — is a little bit wearier: mission accomplished in both respects. "Hey, [pc.MommyDaddy]!" "Hey there, you little rapscallion." You let her jump and flap-flap onto your lap, then give her a hug. "How'd it go with the mail delivery?" "We brought people a bunch of letters! We saw Miss Halima and [annika.numKids 1|Aunt|Miss] Anni and a bunch of ladies I didn't know, and one of them [rand|got so happy that she was crying! Like, good happy! We even got to give her a hug!|looked super — um, the thing that you do when you think something bad is going to happen but it doesn't? That!|thought I did a really good job with the mail delivery! She even gave me a treat!]" You know better than to interrupt the stories, so you let her wax lyrical about mail delivery until she reaches the last recipient. "And then we found Miss Zuzhka who's always the last person on the list and then we came here!" She flops forward to rest on your [pc.belly] and grins up at you. "All done." "All done," Eira confirms. "She did a very good job! I'm always happy to have my mail-delivering friend with me." She turns back to the divine messenger. "Thank you for letting me help, [eira.anyKids|Aunt|Miss] Eira!" [eira.anyKids|"I — oh dear." As ever, your valkyrie lover blushes at being called Aunt anything. ]"Of course, sweetie. I'll see you again later!"

rows.raw: ' "Now, [freja.name]: how will we be making our deliveries today?" Your dragon daughter hefts a bag over her shoulder, neatly cinched so that it doesn't drag on[silly| — haha, dragon dragging on —] the ground. As soon as you arrived at the valkyrie keep and saw Eira, she insisted on helping out: et la voilà. "Super quickly!" she declares. "This is extra important stuff. It's a hero's job!" "Exactly. There's a great deal of mail and my sisters are anxious to receive it!" Eira starts moving down the way toward her first delivery even as she starts speaking. It's a speech you've heard before too, after a fashion. "Imagine if something were going wrong at home for someone in a valkyrie's family..." [freja.name]'s eyes widen for a moment, and then she bolts off to catch up with Eira. You[aileh.wintercity| and Aileh], though, settle down to watch and relax. If the goddess's messenger is ready to be the one to burn off some of your daughter's excess energy, you don't mind taking advantage of the situation. Besides, the ambience is lovely. [aileh.wintercity |Next to you, your draconic lover rests a head on your shoulder and snuggles in. "Do you think Eira's a genius?" Across the hall, you watch as the divine messenger and dragon helper emerge at breakneck speed from one side passage and rush for another. "[pc.isBimbo|Yipyup! And she's a real cutie. You're tryna get [freja.name] to be this good about chores back home — is that going okay|She might be. Any luck on getting [freja.name] to treat her other chores this way]?" She laughs. "Mixed results, dear heart. Same as before: she does everything she's supposed to. She just grumbles and goes a little bit slow." "Work is work." You smooch her on the cheek. "I still [silly|view it as an absolute|call that a] win." So, with amusement and not a small amount of awe, you watch your daughter periodically emerge into the hall, pelting after Eira as fast as she can go, using her wingies to add tiny boosts of speed and somehow avoiding the other valkyries into the bargain — although they're all agile enough to clear out of the way when your little terror comes hurtling their way. For her part, your dear heart spends most of the time relaxing right with you. Once, when [rand|Annika|Thrud|Lumia] drifts by, you three chat about things mundane and serious, but for the most part you sit with each other and enjoy the spectacle. |As you sit back and relax, the Dawn Maiden herself emerges to watch with you. "Taking a break?" You smile. "[pc.isBimbo|Uh-huh! She's got so much energy in her! It's a good thing Eira's helping out with handling it.|If Eira's willing to run some of the energy out of her...]" "And by doing work, no less," she laughs. "If only all of your little one's chores required running, hmm?" "[pc.isBimbo|Yeahhhh. She does what Mommy says, but she pouts about it too. It's kinda like me!|We've been working on that. She's good about doing everything she's supposed to. She just grumbles all the time, which... that's fair.]" You turn back to see your daughter emerge from a side passage, bag noticeably lighter, pelting hell bent for leather after Eira. "At least this is a little more fun for her." "Every time you visit, I can't help but think of what a wonderful job the three of you have done," the goddess says. "You're a good [pc.mf|father|mother], [pc.name]." "[pc.isBimbo|Thank youuuu!|Thanks.]" From across the hall, you see your daughter bounce up, letter in hand, and hand it to a smiling valkyrie. You can see the smile from across the hall, too. "[pc.isBimbo|I got super lucky with my family.|I've been lucky.]" ] You've relaxed and conversed for quite a while by the time [freja.name] bounds back your way. Her bag is lighter and her step — somehow — is a little bit wearier: mission accomplished in both respects. "Hey, [pc.MommyDaddy]!" "Hey there, you little rapscallion." You let her jump and flap-flap onto your lap, then give her a hug. "How'd it go with the mail delivery?" "We brought people a bunch of letters! We saw Miss Halima and [annika.numKids 1|Aunt|Miss] Anni and a bunch of ladies I didn't know, and one of them [rand|got so happy that she was crying! Like, good happy! We even got to give her a hug!|looked super — um, the thing that you do when you think something bad is going to happen but it doesn't? That!|thought I did a really good job with the mail delivery! She even gave me a treat!]" You know better than to interrupt the stories, so you let her wax lyrical about mail delivery until she reaches the last recipient. "And then we found Miss Zuzhka who's always the last person on the list and then we came here!" She flops forward to rest on your [pc.belly] and grins up at you. "All done." "All done," Eira confirms. "She did a very good job! I'm always happy to have my mail-delivering friend with me." She turns back to the divine messenger. "Thank you for letting me help, [eira.anyKids|Aunt|Miss] Eira!" [eira.anyKids|"I — oh dear." As ever, your valkyrie lover blushes at being called Aunt anything. ]"Of course, sweetie. I'll see you again later!"'

rows.original: [var0 |"Unfortunately sweetie," you begin, scooping [freja.name] up in your arms, regardless of the way it immediately soaks you to hug someone who's been melting snow on their body all day. "It's time for us to head home." [freja.name] looks torn between exhaustion, and sadness. "Aww... but—" when her complaint is interrupted by a yawn she relents, snuggling up against you and yawning again. "Okaaaay..." "Did you have a fun time today, sweetie?" "Yes! We should bring mommy next time!" "We will," you promise, heading towards the main gate. You can see that a few caravans are getting ready to return to whence they came, and a few familiar folk give you a wave. "Well, looks like we have our ride home, too." You and [freja.name] hop up onto one of the wagons, being pulled by a grumpy-looking horse covered in blankets, and get ready for the journey back... of course, by the time you've even traveled for ten minutes, your daughter's fallen asleep. She hums and hisses happily while you brush out her hair, and giggles a little in her sleep when you clean up her claw[silly|b]s, but otherwise it's a peaceful return to the Wayfort. The dragonling only wakes up again when you're hopping down, and is scooped up into Aileh's arms for a big snuggle. Your draconic girlfriend leans in and gives you a kiss, smiling warmly. "Have fun, you two?" "Yess..." [freja.name] mumbles sleepily, snuggling up. Aileh leans in, hugging [freja.name] between the two of you so that she can share a kiss. "I have missed you both like crazy. How about we get [freja.name] tucked away, and have a little personal time?" |[aileh.wintercity|You and Aileh are still holding [freja.name]'s hands, when Aileh finally crouches down and strokes the dragonling's hair. [freja.name] beams a heart-melting smile at the both of you, releasing your respective hands so that she can leap into Aileh's embrace and snuggle into her chest. [party.has etheryn
        |As your party is about to step into Ryn's throne room, you're greeted by the guards giving their regent a sharp nod as she makes to enter.
        
        "Regent." 
        
        "Is something the matter?"
        
        "There is. Not too long ago, a druidic schismatic arrived at the palace, very pointedly requesting to see you — as part of a delegation, I'm given to understand. Since you were out with the champion and absent, her case has so far been handled by the high priestess over the last day or two. You can imagine how that has turned out."
        
        [etheryn.lnhConfidence
            |"O-oh dear. I guess I'd better hurry in and see what can be done. It's a good thing we didn't arrive any later than we did, [pc.name] — c-could you please help me with this? I'll admit to being a little nervous."
            
            You can tell Ryn's more than a little nervous — she's practically shaking in her boots at the thought of having to deal with what must no doubt be a prickly situation. Nevertheless, she's right — it's got to be dealt with.
            |Ryn sighs at that, prompting an indignant squawk from Harrick on her shoulder. "That can't be good. Elthara dealing with the druids — I can only imagine the ruckus they've caused while I was out with [pc.name]."
            
            "It is a delicate diplomatic situation, Regent."
            
            "And how. Come on, [pc.name] — would you mind backing me up on this? I think I'll need the help."
            |Ryn audibly groans at that, prompting a squawk from Harrick. "If there were anyone else save for Elthara who wasn't killed or missing... but no, of all people, of course she has to be the one to deal with the druids out of necessity. This can't be good."
            
            "It is a delicate diplomatic situation, Regent."
            
            "Well, it's up to us to sort out this mess. I can't say I'll relish it, but it has to be done — if not us, then who? And if not now, then when? Come on, [pc.name]. I'll feel a lot better having you at my back."
        ]
        
        The guards nod and push open the door as they step aside, allowing you in. As you make your entrance, you're greeted by the sight of Elthara in her full high priestess' regalia, speaking sharply with Hethia by the throne while the druidess' warg rests by her side. The druidess herself has also donned what passes for formal wear amongst her kind, you suppose — a wreath of evergreen sprigs adorns her brow in addition to her white shift, and she's even been allowed to keep her weapon, no doubt a sign of goodwill, for all that it's worth. The two elven women are caught up in the midst of a heated argument, and only stop when they notice Ryn sweep past them and seat herself with a sigh atop the throne.
        
        Now then... 
        |As you're about to step into Ryn's throne room, you're greeted by the guards crossing their halberds over the ingress, barring your path.
        
        "The regent is meeting with the druidic schismatics right now," one of the amazonian warrior women states in a dry, flat tone. "It's a delicate diplomatic situation, and tensions are running deep. Please, champion, turn around and return in an hour or two. As renowned as you are for saving the city, this is a matter meant to be handled between the boer'alvar because of the cultural tensions involved."
        
        No sooner are the words out of the guard's mouth that Ryn's voice calls from within. "[etheryn.lnhConfidence
            |I-is that you, [pc.name]? Thank the gods you're here; I was really hoping you'd show up. Guards, p-please let the champion in[party.hasCompanions
                | along with [pc.hisHer] entourage
            ].
            |Is that you there, [pc.name]? Guards, let the champion in[party.hasCompanions
                | along with [pc.hisHer] entourage
            ]. There are no secrets between us, and I'd like [pc.himHer] to advise me during these deliberations. 
            |Is that you I hear beyond the door, [pc.name]? You came at just the right time — while things are going smoothly, I'd like to have you weigh in; the neutral perspective of an outsider who isn't so close to the matter may be useful. Guards, admit the champion[party.hasCompanions
                | along with [pc.hisHer] entourage
            ].
        ]"
        
        The guard who stopped you bites her lip at Ryn's direct contradiction of her words, but the both of them uncross their halberds and step aside, pushing open the door to Ryn's throne room. As you make your entrance, you're greeted by the sight of Etheryn clothed in all of her royal splendour, and Hethia kneeling before the throne, her warg lying on the carpet at her side. The druidess herself has also donned what passes for formal wear amongst her kind, you suppose — a wreath of evergreen sprigs adorns her brow in addition to her white shift, and she's even been allowed to keep her weapon while receiving an audience from Ryn. That hasn't served to ease the tension coming from the guards in the least, but Ryn herself seems at ease as she welcomes you and bids for you to step forward to her side. You throw a glance up at the galleries, but none of the Winter City's upper crust are in attendance; this must be a private audience — the only other person aside from the guards is Ryn's high priestess of Lumia, Elthara, by her side to the throne's left.
        
        What's going on?
    ]

[party.has etheryn
        |当你的队伍即将走进瑞恩的王座厅时，守卫们向这位摄政王恭敬地点了点头，让她得以进入。

“摄政王。”

“有什么事情吗？”

“确实有事情。 不久前，一位德鲁伊派的分裂者来到了宫殿，她明确表示想要见你——据我所知，她是作为代表团的一员前来拜访的。由于你当时正与那位英雄在一起，不在宫殿里，所以在过去一两天里，她的事情是由大祭司来处理的。 你可以想象结果会是怎样的。
        
        [etheryn.lnhConfidence
            |哦，天哪。我想我最好赶紧进去看看能做些什么。幸好我们没有晚到。 [pc.name] 您能帮帮我吗？我得承认，我有点紧张。”

从Ryn的表现来看，她的紧张程度显然不轻——一想到要处理这个肯定棘手的问题，她几乎都在发抖了。不过，她说得对，这个问题必须得解决。
            |听到这话，瑞恩叹了口气，她肩上的哈里克立刻发出愤怒的叫声：“那肯定不是什么好事。艾尔塔拉正在和那些德鲁伊打交道……我只能想象，在我不在的时候，他们肯定惹出了一堆麻烦。 [pc.name]这确实是一个微妙的外交局面，摄政王。”

“是啊，真是如此。来吧，继续说吧 [pc.name] 你能不能在这件事上支持我一下？我想我确实需要帮助。
            |听到这话，瑞恩明显发出了呻吟声，这让哈里克忍不住抱怨道：“要是除了埃尔萨拉之外，还有其他人没有死或者没有失踪该多好……但偏偏就是她，出于种种原因，不得不去处理那些德鲁伊的事情。这肯定不是什么好事。”

“这确实是一个棘手的外交问题，摄政王。”

“好吧，解决这个麻烦事就落在我们身上了。虽然我并不乐意这么做，但这件事必须得完成——如果不是我们，那还能有谁来处理？如果不在现在，那还能等到什么时候？快点吧。 [pc.name]有你在我身边，我会感觉安心多了。
        ]
        
        守卫们点头示意，然后退到一旁推开门让你进去。当你走进门时，首先映入眼帘的是身着高级女祭司礼服的埃尔萨拉，她正站在王座旁严厉地与赫希娅交谈，而那位德鲁伊的女战士则站在她的身边。 这位女德鲁伊也应该穿上了她族群认为属于正式场合的服装吧——除了那件白色的长袍外，她的额头上还戴着一圈常青女士枝编成的花环。而且，她甚至被允许保留自己的武器，这无疑是一种善意的表示，尽管这种善意可能并不值得过分看重。 那两位精灵女子正陷入激烈的争论之中，直到她们注意到瑞恩从她们身边掠过，然后叹着气坐上了王座，这场争论才停止。

那么……现在该怎么做呢？ 
        |当你即将走进瑞恩的王座厅时，守卫们将长矛横在入口处，阻住了你的去路。

“摄政王现在正在与那些分裂派德鲁伊会面，”其中一位亚马逊女战士用冰冷、平板的语气说道。 这是一个非常微妙的外交局势，紧张局势正在不断加剧。拜托了，冠军，一两个小时后再回来吧。尽管你以拯救这座城市而闻名，但鉴于其中涉及的文化矛盾，这件事应该由布尔人自己来处理。还没等卫兵把话说完，里恩的声音就从里面传了出来：[etheryn.lnhConfidence
            |是你吗？ [pc.name]? 多亏了你来了，我真希望你会出现。卫兵们，请让这位冠军进来吧。[party.hasCompanions
                | 以及 [pc.hisHer] 随从团队
            ].
            |是你吗？ [pc.name]? 守卫们，让这位冠军进来吧。[party.hasCompanions
                | 以及 [pc.hisHer] 随行人员
            ]我们之间没有任何秘密，我想 [pc.himHer] 在这些讨论过程中给予我建议。 
            |是我听到的那声音吗，来自门的那边？ [pc.name]? 你来得正是时候——既然目前一切进展顺利，我想听听你的意见；一个与这件事没有太大关联的旁观者的中立观点可能会很有帮助。卫兵们，把冠军交出来吧。[party.hasCompanions
                | 以及 [pc.hisHer] 随从团队
            ].
        ]那个阻止你的守卫，听到瑞恩直接反驳她的话，不由得咬住了嘴唇。不过他们俩都放下了手中的长矛，让开了道路，为你打开了通往瑞恩王座厅的门。当你走进去时，首先映入眼帘的是身着华丽皇袍的伊瑟琳，而赫希娅则跪在王座前，她的战兽就躺在她身旁的地毯上。 这位女德鲁伊想必也穿上了她族群认为属于正式场合的服装——除了穿着白色的长袍外，她的额头上还戴着一圈常青女士枝编成的花环。而且，在接受瑞恩的接见时，她甚至被允许携带自己的武器。 这丝毫没有缓解守卫们带来的紧张气氛，但瑞恩本人却显得很放松，她热情地迎接你，并示意你走到她身边。你抬头望向观众席，却发现冬城的贵族们没有一个在场——显然，这是一场私人会面。除了守卫们，唯一在场的还有瑞恩的高阶女祭司艾尔塔拉，她站在王座的左侧。
        
        发生了什么事？
    ]

rows.original: Ryn takes a deep breath to steady herself. "Remember, [pc.name]? I promised Hethia favorable terms for the druids in their return to the boer'alvar, if she helped reveal Alissa for the monster that she'd become. Now that all of that's over, it's time for me to make good on my promise. Hethia upheld her half of the deal, and fulfilled her service to the utmost extent of her ability. In that, the druids have shown goodwill in healing the schism in our people... now it's my turn to show them the var Ridells aren't as bad as they imagine us to be." "Mm, that is correct," the druidess says as she bows her head. "Once the terms of our return are finalised, the healing can begin. Queen or Regent, a ruler's words carry much weight — as we are all learning now. Your sister, by all accounts, was rather lackadaisical about what she said, even in public. Everyone is waiting and watching to see how the new Queen — pardon, I meant Regent, for now — will turn out to be. I'm sure that you'll eventually apprehend Alissa, regardless of where she may have fled." "You're quite loose with your tongue, schismatic," Elthara, the high priestess of Lumia, says from Ryn's other side. "Watch your words in front of the regent." "[etheryn.lnhConfidence |P-please, High Priestess. Don't make it any more awkward t-than it has to be. Hethia has stuck her neck out for us and shown faith in [pc.name] and I where she had no need to." Ryn looks like she's going to have a panic attack right now, but swallows hard and forces herself onwards. "She's earned the privilege of being familiar with me by fighting for my cause, if nothing else. |Please don't, High Priestess. We're trying to make peace here — don't make the situation any more awkward than it has to be." Ryn sighs and lets her shoulders sag, then picks herself up and forges onward. "I'd say that by fighting for my cause and the Winter City, she's earned the privilege of being familiar with me. It feels right, after she's stuck her neck out for us. |And who gave you permission to speak out of turn, High Priestess? We're dealing with a delicate diplomatic situation here, with the chance to truly bridge a deep chasm between our peoples. Don't bring your prejudices into this, not after Hethia here's fought for my cause and stuck her neck out for me when she had no reason to." Ryn sighs and rubs her temples. "After such a show of good faith, I think she's earned the privilege of being familiar with me, Regent or no. Am I right? ]" Elthara clears her throat. "Regent, with all respect, when the druids exiled themselves from the Winter City they swore to spill var Ridell blood for abandoning the Old Wyld. Merely two and a half centuries have passed since then. Trust, but verify, as the saying goes. Someone has to be cautious." Well, if they wanted var Ridell blood, they've certainly drawn some of Alissa's. Certainly that should at least slake some of the thirst for revenge that the elven druids had. And let's be frank — given that you ran into Hethia in the Winter City trying to sue for peace, that they were the first ones to reach out instead of the other way around, you'd say that they've mellowed out a lot since then to want to extend the proverbial olive branch. Ryn smiles at you. "[etheryn.lnhConfidence |Thanks, [pc.name]. You see, Elthara? Even [pc.name] agrees with me; people r-really can change |Thanks for speaking up, [pc.name]. It's great to know you've got my back |My thanks, [pc.name]. This is why I keep a champion like you around ]. But yes, Elthara, it may have been but two and a half centuries, but that isn't as short a time as we might imagine — if I learned anything after escaping from my sister's clutches, it's that other peoples have far shorter memories than we do — and that includes grudges. Imagine my surprise when I spoke with the baroness of the Marches and discovered that not only was the treaty we had with them defunct, the backing authority had completely collapsed. And we will have to deal with other peoples going forward — the Winter City isn't capable of fighting this alone. If not for [pc.name] and everything I've learned on my travels with [pc.himHer], the Winter City would have been subverted from the inside by that demoness. "We need to gather resources and form alliances, Elthara. That begins with our own people. If we can convince a good chunk of our own to reunite from exile and overcome bad blood, convincing other peoples will be easy by comparison." "This is why Archdruid Xadaron isn't here, and I am," Hethia says. "There's still too much bad blood — one look at Elthara, and they'd be at each other's throats, with no hope of reconciliation." The high priestess quirks an eyebrow. "The Xadaron line still leads the druids, then? History's recorded that Vaeril Xadaron had some choice words for the entire Winter City back then for betraying the old faiths." "His granddaughter. Vaeril and his temple were consumed by... something shortly after we left for the Frostwood. A fungal blight of some sort. She blames the var Ridells and the newly formed Lumian priesthood for his death." "Back to the point," Ryn continues, turning back to Hethia. "Let us talk about the return of the schismatics. As you pointed out, I promised favorable terms." "That is right, Regent. But to facilitate negotiations, let me put on the table what we're willing to do. As you know, the Old Wyld is fading fast, and the Wyld Trees have instructed us to swallow our pride and reunite with the Winter City; save ourselves as our powers disappear, taken by this new foreign people who have moved into the Frostwood and are turning the natural forces to their side. We... we will renounce our dead — dying — religion and once more become your subjects with all the obligations thereof; you will rule us and see to your ancient duties to us. We will... not cause trouble for you or your reign, and will live our lives and reintroduce ourselves to this society as best as we can. "In exchange, we want assurance that we will not be harassed or be subject to prejudice for the decisions that we made in response to your grandmother's decree, that we will not be mocked in the streets or made to participate in any number of ritual humiliations. We have been told to surrender, but at least we are to surrender with dignity. That's not too much to ask, I hope." "It's not," Ryn replies. "But it is a request that's painted with a very broad brush and subject to extreme interpretation. We'll need to work out the details further in private later on, but what do the two of you think? Elthara? [pc.name]?" Ryn's gaze falls upon you, as hard and searching as someone like her is able to muster. She still needs a lot more practice... but she'll get there eventually. [pc.isDK |Well, if your opinion is being asked here, you're sure that Ryn's giving far more generous terms here than you'd have given. If it were up to you, you'd have demanded nothing less than complete and unconditional surrender, just to make a point. She should really take Ryn's offer as-is — she's basically giving Hethia everything she wants, especially when the druids by all appearances are in a very poor bargaining position compared to the crown. |Well, if you're being asked for your opinion, Ryn's being very generous — she's basically giving Hethia everything she wants, especially when the druids by all appearances are in a very poor bargaining position compared to the crown. Even if Ryn isn't the vindictive kind, you'd have expected both parties to hedge their bets before negotiating, but it looks like she just wants this to go as smoothly as possible, and that bodes well for the reunification. ] "And you, Elthara? Anything else to add?" The priestess coughs lightly, clearing her throat. "I do have one question. Does your renunciation of the Old Wyld mean that the schismatics will turn to the light of Lumia?" Something flickers behind Hethia's eyes — doubt, anger, exhaustion. She looks from Ryn, to you, then down to her warg by her side. "I don't know." Ryn thins her lips. "[etheryn.lnhConfidence |C-could you explain? |I'm not sure what you mean. |Come again? ]" "Just because the Wyld Trees have told us to turn away from them doesn't mean we'll bow before this human goddess of light from the south. Some of us may do so, in our own time and for our own reasons, but I won't speak for anyone else. Even with what has happened to Alissa, what with her banishment and all, some of the hardliners are not quite appeased, and would not have gone on if not for the direct command of the Wyld Trees. Asking us to convert all at once... may be a little too much to ask of us, too soon." "I think this is fair," Ryn replies with a nod. "Faith cannot be forced. Elthara, your own will not actively proselytize to them unasked, but if any of them wish to learn more about the light of Lumia, provide them with everything they need to set them upon the proper path. We will not insult their loss, and meet them halfway. [etheryn.lnhConfidence |If you, um, don't mind hearing me out? |I think I have an idea. |Well, I think I have a proposal for you, druidess. ]" "Regent." "All this will have to be done by degrees — the Winter City cannot accommodate all of you at once, not after the destruction the Godswar wrought on both the city itself and its people. The return of your people to the fold will take some time, and you on your part will need to readjust to living in the Winter City. We will need to expand the walls, build new homes for those who wish to live within, ensure that you all can be fed, made comfortable, and do useful work. While this is happening, you will be provided accommodations in the palace and stay on to oversee the reunification process and advise me as to the sensibilities of your — no, our people. Given that you're the best candidate for the task, druidess, it only makes sense. Will you accept?" "This... is a reasonable outcome, Regent." "I'm glad you think of it that way. No one's likely to get everything they want, but we're all trying to be reasonable and work towards the same goals here. Now, this audience is over — you may return to the other druids and inform them of the good news, then return to the palace and get settled in. Champion, a moment of your time, if you please — I would have words with you." Hmm? Your thoughts are cut short, though, as Ryn rises from her throne, takes you by the arm and [etheryn.lnhConfidence |nervously tugs you towards the door on the far end of the throne room that opens to the hallway to her private quarters. The moment it closes, the thin facade of bravery and confidence she had while speaking with Hethia collapses and she sags against you in relief. "Phew," Ryn says, heaving a sigh of relief. "T-that really took it out of me... it's hard, having to pretend throughout all of that." Heavy is the head that wears the crown — she already knew that, you suppose, but it's hard to imagine what it's like until you experience it for yourself. "Alissa made it all look so easy, but even she hated it. Although it was for different reasons, I guess. Thanks for being around for me, [pc.name] — half of the time I don't even know what I'm doing. Just having you around makes me think of what you might do, and I go with that; I know I'm not very good at anything so I shouldn't come up with my own ideas anyway because they're just bound to mess things up." |gently tugs you towards the door on the far end of the throne room that opens to the hallway to her private quarters.. Once the both of you are alone, her mask of calm fades and she heaves a small sigh. "Phew. That was tiring. I know I'm getting more and more used to this ruling business, but I feel like I'm treading on eggshells all the time and it really takes it out of me." Treading on eggshells is putting it lightly — like back there with Hethia, one wrong move would have jeopardised the entirety of the reunification process. Heavy is the head that wears the crown, as they say, but someone's got to make these decisions and better her than her sister calling the shots around here; even if she's less capable for now, she nevertheless has her own people in mind. Best a chance of failure than certain deliberate sabotage. "Alissa made it look all so easy — when she could bother with being royal, I guess..." From everything you've seen of her sister, she was plenty capable but disinclined to use her talents as they should have. That, as far as you're concerned, is worse than someone who's floundering but at least doing her best to improve and do the right thing. Ryn gives you a small smile. "T-thanks, [pc.name]. I really appreciate having you around at these times. When you backed me up... I felt like I was on even footing with Hethia there." |leads you out towards the door on the far end of the throne room leading to the private quarters, not looking back. The moment it closes behind the both of you, Ryn sighs, lets her shoulders sag and gives you a rueful smile. Long day, you take it? "Long enough. I've got so many people helping me, especially Elthara, and I'm really glad for you showing up back there when you did. Hethia's not even the worst encounter I've had by far ever since becoming Regent — at least she genuinely wants to work with me. Ruling is pretty exhausting." Heavy is the head that wears the crown — she already knew that, you suppose, but it's hard to imagine what it's like until you experience it for yourself. Ryn nods in agreement. "Alissa made it look all so easy — when she could be bothered to take on the mantle of royalty. I know I'm the better choice compared to her, but even so, there are some days where I wish I had her charisma. Even when she didn't know what she was doing, she always managed to appear as if she did." And look at where it led her. Alissa doesn't look like the type who would admit she would ever make a mistake, so naturally she ended up learning nothing. Ryn, on the other hand, can learn and grow. Ryn takes your hand in hers and gives it a squeeze. "Thanks, [pc.name]. It's nice to be reminded that I made the right choice in picking you as a champion. We were all walking on eggshells back there — even I knew what was at stake. And Elthara, although she's not a bad person, does have her blind spots when it comes to the druids, and the same thing goes in reverse. All in all... I know you didn't say that much, [pc.name], but thanks for showing up when you did and being there for me. It really means a lot." ] No problem. So, about Hethia... A sigh. "That's the first step there, I think. Like I said back there, the exact details of the druids' return will need to be hammered out in the coming days, and we'll certainly end up meeting them somewhere in the middle. The only question is how much one side's going to compromise with the other. From the reactions of otherwise good people like Elthara, it's going to be an uphill battle. "But Hethia's our best bet at this point. We'll have guest quarters prepared for her, and from there, arrange for audiences with the rest of her people with her present as a mediator. We intend to make the process quick as possible, after all. Given that the two of you have a good history, if you could visit her, predispose her to being more open-minded to our way of seeing things... I wouldn't mind, either." Well, that's something for you to work on. [party.has Etheryn |"Well, I'm going to go back in, tie up a few loose ends, and then I'll be back with you." She isn't going to stay, oversee the reunification talks? "I would... but I'm going to say I'll be glad to be out there with you, [pc.name]. I don't envy Elthara in her position, but I do trust her to do what's best for the pale elves and not let any of her prejudices come into play. I'm sure even the druids can understand that given what happened in the Winter City, hunting down Kasyrra is rightfully the Regent's top priority. Now, if you'll give me a moment." With that, Ryn's already heading back to the door, leaving you in the hallway to ponder your options... half an hour passes before she rejoins you with a nod. "All right, [pc.name]. Don't worry about it — Elthara and Hethia will cooperate as best as they can." Well, if she has so much trust in them, who are you to question her judgement? Time for you to be off, then — you've had enough political nonsense for a day. |"All right, I've got to be back in the throne room and finish up the audience, sort things out. Maybe I'll see you later, okay?" With that, Ryn's already heading back to the door, leaving you in the hallway to ponder your options... ]
rows.translation: 瑞恩深吸一口气，努力让自己平静下来。“记住，”她说道。 [pc.name]我曾向赫希娅承诺，如果她帮助揭露艾莉莎真正变成的怪物，那么德鲁伊们重返布尔阿尔瓦尔时将会得到优厚的待遇。现在这一切都已经结束了，是时候履行我的承诺了。 赫希娅履行了自己在协议中应承担的责任，也尽自己最大的能力完成了相关义务。正因如此，德鲁伊们才表现出善意，帮助我们消除了族群之间的分歧……现在，轮到我来向他们证明：拉里德尔家族并没有他们想象中那么糟糕。嗯，没错，”女德鲁伊低头说道，“一旦我们返回的条件确定下来，治疗就可以开始了。无论是女王还是摄政王，统治者的话语都具有很大的分量——这一点我们现在都深有体会。 据大家所说，你妹妹在说话时总是漫不经心，甚至在公共场合也是如此。现在大家都在等着看这位新女王——哦，不对，应该是摄政王——最终会成为一个怎样的人。我相信，无论艾丽莎逃到了哪里，你最终都会找到她的。你说话可真是不留情面啊，分裂者，”卢米亚的大祭司艾尔塔拉从瑞恩的另一侧说道，“在摄政王面前，你可要谨慎言辞。”[etheryn.lnhConfidence |P-求你了，大祭司。别让事情变得更加尴尬了。赫希娅已经为我们挺身而出，表达了她的信任 [pc.name] 而我，根本不需要她这样做。”瑞恩看起来随时都会陷入恐慌，但她强忍住情绪，继续说道：“至少，她为我的事业而奋斗，因此她有这个资格来了解我。 |请不要这样，大祭司。我们正在努力在这里实现和平——请不要让局势变得更加尴尬。”瑞恩叹了口气，肩膀耷了下来，但很快又振作起来，继续前行。“我认为，因为她为我的事业和冬城挺身而出，她已经赢得了与我熟络相处的资格。在她为我们付出这么多之后，这样做似乎也是理所应当的。 |大祭司，谁允许你打断别人说话的？我们现在正处在一个微妙的外交关头，这个机会真的可以弥合我们两国人民之间的隔阂。请不要把你的偏见带到这里来——毕竟赫希娅毫无理由地为我挺身而出，为我奋斗过。瑞恩叹了口气，揉了揉太阳穴：“在她表现出如此诚意之后，我认为她确实应该有权利了解我，无论她是否拥有摄政者的身份。我说得对吧？ ]埃尔萨拉清了清嗓子，说道：“摄政王，恕我直言。当德鲁伊们离开冬城时，他们曾发誓要为那些抛弃古老荒野的人报仇。而从那时起，仅仅过去了两个半世纪而已。 正如那句俗话所说：要相信，但也要核实。总得有人保持警惕才行。 嗯，如果他们真的想要拉里德尔的血液，那么他们肯定已经得到了艾莉莎的一些血液。至少，这应该能够满足那些精灵德鲁伊们的复仇欲望吧。 坦白说，既然你在冬城遇到了赫希娅，当时他们正是试图通过和平谈判来解决问题，而且也是他们主动联系你的，而不是你先去找他们，那么可以认为，从那以后他们的态度已经变得温和了许多，甚至愿意伸出所谓的“橄榄枝”来寻求和解。 瑞恩对你笑了笑。[etheryn.lnhConfidence |谢谢。 [pc.name]你看，埃尔萨拉？就连 [pc.name] 同意我的看法；人确实是能够改变的。 |感谢你站出来发声。 [pc.name]知道你会支持我，真是太好了。 |非常感谢。 [pc.name]这就是为什么我会留着你这样的英雄在身边。 ]但是，没错，埃尔萨拉，虽然那仅仅两个半世纪的时间，但实际上这段距离远比我们想象的要长。如果说我从逃离姐姐的控制中领悟到了什么的话，那就是其他民族的记忆力远不如我们——这种记忆力包括他们对过去的怨恨与恩怨。当你与我交谈那位边境女男爵时，你一定能想象到我当时的惊讶：我们与他们签订的条约早已失效，而支撑这些条约的权威机构也彻底崩溃了。我们 会 今后我们必须应对其他势力的挑战——冬城独自无力应对这样的挑战。要不是有 [pc.name] 以及我在这些旅行中所学到的一切。 [pc.himHer]如果那样的女恶魔得逞，冬城早就从内部被颠覆了。 “我们必须筹集资源并结成联盟，埃尔萨拉。这一切首先要从我们自己的族人开始。如果我们能说服大部分流亡在外的族人回归家园，消除彼此之间的怨恨，那么说服其他族人就会变得容易多了。 这就是为什么大德鲁伊扎达伦不在这里，而我在的原因，”赫希娅说道，“他们之间的怨恨仍然太深了——只要看一眼埃尔萨拉，他们就会立刻互相攻击，根本不可能和解。” 大祭司微微挑了挑眉毛：“那么，扎达伦家族仍然领导着德鲁伊们吗？历史上记载，瓦瑞尔·扎达伦当时曾对整个冬城发表过激烈的批评，指责他们背叛了古老的信仰。 他的孙女瓦雷尔，以及他的神庙，在我们前往冰原森林后不久，就被某种东西毁掉了。是一种真菌病害。她将他的死归咎于里德尔家族以及新成立的卢米安神职人员。” “回到正题，”莱恩继续说道，转向赫希娅，“让我们来谈谈那些分裂派成员的回归问题。正如你指出的，我承诺会给予他们优厚的条件。 没错，摄政王。但为了便于谈判，让我先说明我们愿意做出的让步。如您所知，古老的荒野正在迅速消亡，而那些荒野之树也指示我们放下傲慢，与冬城重新联合起来；因为我们的力量正在逐渐消失，那些新来的外来者已经进入了霜木之地，并将自然力量据为己有。 我们……我们将抛弃我们那早已衰落、濒临灭亡的宗教，再次成为你们的子民，承担起所有相应的义务；你们将统治我们，履行你们对我们一直以来承担的责任。我们……不会给你们或你们的统治带来任何麻烦，会尽我们所能过好自己的生活，重新融入这个社会。 作为交换，我们要求得到保证：对于我们根据您祖母的命令所做出的决定，我们不会受到骚扰或歧视；在街上也不会被人嘲笑，也不会被迫参与任何形式的羞辱性仪式。虽然我们被要求投降，但至少我们应该有尊严地投降。我希望，这并不是过分的要求。 不是这样的，”瑞恩回答道，“但这个请求的表述相当笼统，因此可能会被人们过度解读。我们之后需要私下里进一步讨论细节，不过你们俩怎么看？埃尔萨拉？ [pc.name]莱恩的目轻型落在了你身上，那目轻型坚定而充满探究，一个像她这样的人已经竭尽全力去表达这种目轻型了。她还需要更多的练习……但最终她一定会做到的。 [pc.isDK |嗯，如果这里是在征求你的意见的话，那你肯定应该知道，Ryn提出的条件比你原本会要求的要宽松得多。如果由你来决定，你至少会要求对方无条件投降，这样才能达到你的目的。她真的应该接受Ryn的提议——因为Ryn基本上满足了赫希娅所有的要求。尤其是考虑到德鲁伊们与王室相比，显然处于非常不利的谈判地位。 |嗯，如果有人在征求你的意见的话，我觉得瑞恩确实非常大方——她基本上满足了赫希娅所有的要求。尤其是考虑到德鲁伊们与王室相比显然处于非常不利的谈判地位，瑞恩的做法更是令人印象深刻。即使瑞恩并不是那种喜欢报复的人，但在谈判之前，双方通常都会采取一些策略来保护自己的利益，但看起来她只是希望整个过程能够尽可能顺利地进行，而这对于国家的统一来说，无疑是一个好兆头。 ] 那么你呢，埃尔萨拉？还有什么要补充的吗？” 女祭司轻咳了一声，清了清嗓子：“我确实有一个问题。你放弃旧荒野的意义，是否意味着那些分裂派会转向卢米亚的轻型明呢？” 赫希娅的眼中闪过一丝复杂的神情——怀疑、愤怒，还有疲惫。她的目轻型在莱恩和你之间游移，最后落在了她身旁的战兽身上。 “我不知道。” 莱恩紧抿着嘴唇，没有再说话。[etheryn.lnhConfidence |你能解释一下吗？ |我不太明白你的意思。 |什么？你说什么？ ]仅仅因为荒野之树告诉我们要远离它们，并不意味着我们要向这位来自南方的轻型明女神屈服。我们中有些人可能会在适当的时候，出于自己的原因这样做，但我不能代表其他人来表态。 尽管发生了那些事情，尽管阿丽莎被流放了，但一些强硬派人士仍然不满意，如果不是因为野树的直接命令，他们也不会罢休。他们要求我们立即完成所有的转换工作。这对我们来说，可能要求有点太高了，而且也太早了。” “我认为这是公平的，”瑞恩点头说道，“信仰是不能强迫的。埃尔萨拉，你也不会主动去向他们传播信仰，但如果他们中有任何人想要了解更多关于卢米亚之轻型的信息，那就为他们提供一切所需的条件，帮助他们走上正确的道路。 我们不会嘲笑他们的失败，而是会采取折中的态度与他们相处。 [etheryn.lnhConfidence |如果你，嗯，不介意听我讲完的话？ |我想我有个主意了。 |嗯，德鲁伊女士，我想我有一个建议可以提给你。 ]摄政王。” “这一切都必须循序渐进地进行——在神战对这座城市及其居民造成了如此巨大的破坏之后，冬城根本无法同时容纳你们所有人。 让你的子民重新回归家园需要一些时间，而你们自己也需要重新适应在冬城的生活。我们必须加高城墙，为那些愿意居住在这里的人建造新的房屋，确保大家都有食物吃，生活舒适，并且能够从事有意义的工作。 在这段时间里，你将被安排住在宫殿里，继续负责监督重新统一的过程，并根据你那一方的实际情况向我提供建议——不，应该是 我们的 人们。既然你是完成这项任务的最佳人选，德鲁伊女士，那么这个决定当然是合理的。你愿意接受吗？” “这……确实是一个合理的结果，摄政王。” “我很高兴你也能这么看。没有人能够得到自己想要的一切，但我们都在努力保持理性，为共同的目标而努力。 现在，这位听众已经听完了——你们可以回去告诉其他德鲁伊这个好消息，然后回到宫殿安顿下来。冠军，请您稍等片刻，我有话要跟您说。嗯？不过，你的思绪被打断了——因为瑞恩从王座上站起来，抓住了你的手臂，然后 [etheryn.lnhConfidence |她紧张地拉着你走向王座厅尽头的那扇门，那扇门通向通往她私人居室的走廊。门一关上，她在与赫希娅交谈时表现出的那种勇敢和自信的外表立刻消失了，她松懈地靠在你身上，仿佛如释重负。 呼，”瑞恩松了一口气说道，“真的让我精疲力竭了……在整个过程中一直假装自己是什么样的人，实在太难了。” “戴王冠的人责任重大”——你或许早就知道这个道理，但直到真正体验过，才真正能理解那意味着什么。 艾丽莎把这一切都表现得如此轻松，但就连她自己也不喜欢这样做。当然，原因可能各不相同吧。谢谢你一直在我身边支持我。 [pc.name] 有一半的时间，我甚至都不知道自己在做什么。只要有你在身边，我就会想到你可能会怎么做，然后我就跟着你的思路来；我知道自己什么都不太擅长，所以本来就不应该自己想主意，因为那些主意肯定只会把事情搞砸。 rows.raw: " Ryn takes a deep breath to steady herself. "Remember, [pc.name]? I promised Hethia favorable terms for the druids in their return to the boer'alvar, if she helped reveal Alissa for the monster that she'd become. Now that all of that's over, it's time for me to make good on my promise. Hethia upheld her half of the deal, and fulfilled her service to the utmost extent of her ability. In that, the druids have shown goodwill in healing the schism in our people... now it's my turn to show them the var Ridells aren't as bad as they imagine us to be." "Mm, that is correct," the druidess says as she bows her head. "Once the terms of our return are finalised, the healing can begin. Queen or Regent, a ruler's words carry much weight — as we are all learning now. Your sister, by all accounts, was rather lackadaisical about what she said, even in public. Everyone is waiting and watching to see how the new Queen — pardon, I meant Regent, for now — will turn out to be. I'm sure that you'll eventually apprehend Alissa, regardless of where she may have fled." "You're quite loose with your tongue, schismatic," Elthara, the high priestess of Lumia, says from Ryn's other side. "Watch your words in front of the regent." "[etheryn.lnhConfidence |P-please, High Priestess. Don't make it any more awkward t-than it has to be. Hethia has stuck her neck out for us and shown faith in [pc.name] and I where she had no need to." Ryn looks like she's going to have a panic attack right now, but swallows hard and forces herself onwards. "She's earned the privilege of being familiar with me by fighting for my cause, if nothing else. |Please don't, High Priestess. We're trying to make peace here — don't make the situation any more awkward than it has to be." Ryn sighs and lets her shoulders sag, then picks herself up and forges onward. "I'd say that by fighting for my cause and the Winter City, she's earned the privilege of being familiar with me. It feels right, after she's stuck her neck out for us. |And who gave you permission to speak out of turn, High Priestess? We're dealing with a delicate diplomatic situation here, with the chance to truly bridge a deep chasm between our peoples. Don't bring your prejudices into this, not after Hethia here's fought for my cause and stuck her neck out for me when she had no reason to." Ryn sighs and rubs her temples. "After such a show of good faith, I think she's earned the privilege of being familiar with me, Regent or no. Am I right? ]" Elthara clears her throat. "Regent, with all respect, when the druids exiled themselves from the Winter City they swore to spill var Ridell blood for abandoning the Old Wyld. Merely two and a half centuries have passed since then. Trust, but verify, as the saying goes. Someone has to be cautious." Well, if they wanted var Ridell blood, they've certainly drawn some of Alissa's. Certainly that should at least slake some of the thirst for revenge that the elven druids had. And let's be frank — given that you ran into Hethia in the Winter City trying to sue for peace, that they were the first ones to reach out instead of the other way around, you'd say that they've mellowed out a lot since then to want to extend the proverbial olive branch. Ryn smiles at you. "[etheryn.lnhConfidence |Thanks, [pc.name]. You see, Elthara? Even [pc.name] agrees with me; people r-really can change |Thanks for speaking up, [pc.name]. It's great to know you've got my back |My thanks, [pc.name]. This is why I keep a champion like you around ]. But yes, Elthara, it may have been but two and a half centuries, but that isn't as short a time as we might imagine — if I learned anything after escaping from my sister's clutches, it's that other peoples have far shorter memories than we do — and that includes grudges. Imagine my surprise when I spoke with the baroness of the Marches and discovered that not only was the treaty we had with them defunct, the backing authority had completely collapsed. And we will have to deal with other peoples going forward — the Winter City isn't capable of fighting this alone. If not for [pc.name] and everything I've learned on my travels with [pc.himHer], the Winter City would have been subverted from the inside by that demoness. "We need to gather resources and form alliances, Elthara. That begins with our own people. If we can convince a good chunk of our own to reunite from exile and overcome bad blood, convincing other peoples will be easy by comparison." "This is why Archdruid Xadaron isn't here, and I am," Hethia says. "There's still too much bad blood — one look at Elthara, and they'd be at each other's throats, with no hope of reconciliation." The high priestess quirks an eyebrow. "The Xadaron line still leads the druids, then? History's recorded that Vaeril Xadaron had some choice words for the entire Winter City back then for betraying the old faiths." "His granddaughter. Vaeril and his temple were consumed by... something shortly after we left for the Frostwood. A fungal blight of some sort. She blames the var Ridells and the newly formed Lumian priesthood for his death." "Back to the point," Ryn continues, turning back to Hethia. "Let us talk about the return of the schismatics. As you pointed out, I promised favorable terms." "That is right, Regent. But to facilitate negotiations, let me put on the table what we're willing to do. As you know, the Old Wyld is fading fast, and the Wyld Trees have instructed us to swallow our pride and reunite with the Winter City; save ourselves as our powers disappear, taken by this new foreign people who have moved into the Frostwood and are turning the natural forces to their side. We... we will renounce our dead — dying — religion and once more become your subjects with all the obligations thereof; you will rule us and see to your ancient duties to us. We will... not cause trouble for you or your reign, and will live our lives and reintroduce ourselves to this society as best as we can. "In exchange, we want assurance that we will not be harassed or be subject to prejudice for the decisions that we made in response to your grandmother's decree, that we will not be mocked in the streets or made to participate in any number of ritual humiliations. We have been told to surrender, but at least we are to surrender with dignity. That's not too much to ask, I hope." "It's not," Ryn replies. "But it is a request that's painted with a very broad brush and subject to extreme interpretation. We'll need to work out the details further in private later on, but what do the two of you think? Elthara? [pc.name]?" Ryn's gaze falls upon you, as hard and searching as someone like her is able to muster. She still needs a lot more practice... but she'll get there eventually. [pc.isDK |Well, if your opinion is being asked here, you're sure that Ryn's giving far more generous terms here than you'd have given. If it were up to you, you'd have demanded nothing less than complete and unconditional surrender, just to make a point. She should really take Ryn's offer as-is — she's basically giving Hethia everything she wants, especially when the druids by all appearances are in a very poor bargaining position compared to the crown. |Well, if you're being asked for your opinion, Ryn's being very generous — she's basically giving Hethia everything she wants, especially when the druids by all appearances are in a very poor bargaining position compared to the crown. Even if Ryn isn't the vindictive kind, you'd have expected both parties to hedge their bets before negotiating, but it looks like she just wants this to go as smoothly as possible, and that bodes well for the reunification. ] "And you, Elthara? Anything else to add?" The priestess coughs lightly, clearing her throat. "I do have one question. Does your renunciation of the Old Wyld mean that the schismatics will turn to the light of Lumia?" Something flickers behind Hethia's eyes — doubt, anger, exhaustion. She looks from Ryn, to you, then down to her warg by her side. "I don't know." Ryn thins her lips. "[etheryn.lnhConfidence |C-could you explain? |I'm not sure what you mean. |Come again? ]" "Just because the Wyld Trees have told us to turn away from them doesn't mean we'll bow before this human goddess of light from the south. Some of us may do so, in our own time and for our own reasons, but I won't speak for anyone else. Even with what has happened to Alissa, what with her banishment and all, some of the hardliners are not quite appeased, and would not have gone on if not for the direct command of the Wyld Trees. Asking us to convert all at once... may be a little too much to ask of us, too soon." "I think this is fair," Ryn replies with a nod. "Faith cannot be forced. Elthara, your own will not actively proselytize to them unasked, but if any of them wish to learn more about the light of Lumia, provide them with everything they need to set them upon the proper path. We will not insult their loss, and meet them halfway. [etheryn.lnhConfidence |If you, um, don't mind hearing me out? |I think I have an idea. |Well, I think I have a proposal for you, druidess. ]" "Regent." "All this will have to be done by degrees — the Winter City cannot accommodate all of you at once, not after the destruction the Godswar wrought on both the city itself and its people. The return of your people to the fold will take some time, and you on your part will need to readjust to living in the Winter City. We will need to expand the walls, build new homes for those who wish to live within, ensure that you all can be fed, made comfortable, and do useful work. While this is happening, you will be provided accommodations in the palace and stay on to oversee the reunification process and advise me as to the sensibilities of your — no, our people. Given that you're the best candidate for the task, druidess, it only makes sense. Will you accept?" "This... is a reasonable outcome, Regent." "I'm glad you think of it that way. No one's likely to get everything they want, but we're all trying to be reasonable and work towards the same goals here. Now, this audience is over — you may return to the other druids and inform them of the good news, then return to the palace and get settled in. Champion, a moment of your time, if you please — I would have words with you." Hmm? Your thoughts are cut short, though, as Ryn rises from her throne, takes you by the arm and [etheryn.lnhConfidence |nervously tugs you towards the door on the far end of the throne room that opens to the hallway to her private quarters. The moment it closes, the thin facade of bravery and confidence she had while speaking with Hethia collapses and she sags against you in relief. "Phew," Ryn says, heaving a sigh of relief. "T-that really took it out of me... it's hard, having to pretend throughout all of that." Heavy is the head that wears the crown — she already knew that, you suppose, but it's hard to imagine what it's like until you experience it for yourself. "Alissa made it all look so easy, but even she hated it. Although it was for different reasons, I guess. Thanks for being around for me, [pc.name] — half of the time I don't even know what I'm doing. Just having you around makes me think of what you might do, and I go with that; I know I'm not very good at anything so I shouldn't come up with my own ideas anyway because they're just bound to mess things up." |gently tugs you towards the door on the far end of the throne room that opens to the hallway to her private quarters.. Once the both of you are alone, her mask of calm fades and she heaves a small sigh. "Phew. That was tiring. I know I'm getting more and more used to this ruling business, but I feel like I'm treading on eggshells all the time and it really takes it out of me." Treading on eggshells is putting it lightly — like back there with Hethia, one wrong move would have jeopardised the entirety of the reunification process. Heavy is the head that wears the crown, as they say, but someone's got to make these decisions and better her than her sister calling the shots around here; even if she's less capable for now, she nevertheless has her own people in mind. Best a chance of failure than certain deliberate sabotage. "Alissa made it look all so easy — when she could bother with being royal, I guess..." From everything you've seen of her sister, she was plenty capable but disinclined to use her talents as they should have. That, as far as you're concerned, is worse than someone who's floundering but at least doing her best to improve and do the right thing. Ryn gives you a small smile. "T-thanks, [pc.name]. I really appreciate having you around at these times. When you backed me up... I felt like I was on even footing with Hethia there." |leads you out towards the door on the far end of the throne room leading to the private quarters, not looking back. The moment it closes behind the both of you, Ryn sighs, lets her shoulders sag and gives you a rueful smile. Long day, you take it? "Long enough. I've got so many people helping me, especially Elthara, and I'm really glad for you showing up back there when you did. Hethia's not even the worst encounter I've had by far ever since becoming Regent — at least she genuinely wants to work with me. Ruling is pretty exhausting." Heavy is the head that wears the crown — she already knew that, you suppose, but it's hard to imagine what it's like until you experience it for yourself. Ryn nods in agreement. "Alissa made it look all so easy — when she could be bothered to take on the mantle of royalty. I know I'm the better choice compared to her, but even so, there are some days where I wish I had her charisma. Even when she didn't know what she was doing, she always managed to appear as if she did." And look at where it led her. Alissa doesn't look like the type who would admit she would ever make a mistake, so naturally she ended up learning nothing. Ryn, on the other hand, can learn and grow. Ryn takes your hand in hers and gives it a squeeze. "Thanks, [pc.name]. It's nice to be reminded that I made the right choice in picking you as a champion. We were all walking on eggshells back there — even I knew what was at stake. And Elthara, although she's not a bad person, does have her blind spots when it comes to the druids, and the same thing goes in reverse. All in all... I know you didn't say that much, [pc.name], but thanks for showing up when you did and being there for me. It really means a lot." ] No problem. So, about Hethia... A sigh. "That's the first step there, I think. Like I said back there, the exact details of the druids' return will need to be hammered out in the coming days, and we'll certainly end up meeting them somewhere in the middle. The only question is how much one side's going to compromise with the other. From the reactions of otherwise good people like Elthara, it's going to be an uphill battle. "But Hethia's our best bet at this point. We'll have guest quarters prepared for her, and from there, arrange for audiences with the rest of her people with her present as a mediator. We intend to make the process quick as possible, after all. Given that the two of you have a good history, if you could visit her, predispose her to being more open-minded to our way of seeing things... I wouldn't mind, either." Well, that's something for you to work on. [party.has Etheryn |"Well, I'm going to go back in, tie up a few loose ends, and then I'll be back with you." She isn't going to stay, oversee the reunification talks? "I would... but I'm going to say I'll be glad to be out there with you, [pc.name]. I don't envy Elthara in her position, but I do trust her to do what's best for the pale elves and not let any of her prejudices come into play. I'm sure even the druids can understand that given what happened in the Winter City, hunting down Kasyrra is rightfully the Regent's top priority. Now, if you'll give me a moment." With that, Ryn's already heading back to the door, leaving you in the hallway to ponder your options... half an hour passes before she rejoins you with a nod. "All right, [pc.name]. Don't worry about it — Elthara and Hethia will cooperate as best as they can." Well, if she has so much trust in them, who are you to question her judgement? Time for you to be off, then — you've had enough political nonsense for a day. |"All right, I've got to be back in the throne room and finish up the audience, sort things out. Maybe I'll see you later, okay?" With that, Ryn's already heading back to the door, leaving you in the hallway to ponder your options... ] "

rows.original:
"You." Hethia's voice is as dry as ever, unchanged from when you confronted her at Westbank over the fate of the loggers. The druidess eyes you up and down "Fancy seeing you here. I'd heard someone from outside of the Winter City happened to be declared the new Champion of Winter, but I didn't expect it to be you. Life is full of surprises, isn't it?"

        [var0
            |"Yes, [pc.himHer]. The three of us meet again, hopefully under more peaceable circumstances this time
            |Ryn purses her lips. "You know [pc.name]?"

            Hethia hesitates, then nods. "We were involved in an altercation over a disagreement recently. Instead of immediately taking arms, [pc.heShe] chose to hear me out and reach a peaceable resolution through negotiation. I... did not expect that from anyone who was not boer'alvar."
            
            That brings a warm, genuine smile to Ryn's face. "Well, how appropriate for what we're discussing today
        ]. Hethia, this is the recently enshrined Champion of Winter, instrumental in revealing my sister's corruption to all of the Winter City, and deposing her wickedness from the throne. I hope you'll give [pc.himHer] all the respect due to [pc.himHer] station."

        The druidess bites her lip and the warg at her side perks up its ears, but she nods. "I see. [pc.Name] has been fair to me as well."
        
        Ryn frowns and eyes you, trying her best to look contemplative and regal. "Well, that's a good start, if nothing else. How much do you know about the schism in the boer'alvar, [pc.name]?"
        
        Hethia told you some of it when you met her down at the logging camp, you remember. She had... less than glowing praise for the Winter City back then.
        
        The druidess swallows hard. "Let not mince words — that is the position that many of us exiles hold, and would still hold if not for recent developments."
        
        "Good, so I don't need to catch you up on that piece of history. On the other hand, these recent developments — for the sake of the Champion of Winter, Emissary, would you please enlighten my champion on those details?"
        
        Hethia winces. "I — Regent, this is — "
        
        At that, Ryn starts speaking to Hethia is what can only be their native tongue. The discussion is quite animated, if hushed, but Hethia eventually nods, even if she looks distinctly unhappy about it all.
        
        "It's fine to tell [pc.name] about it?" the druidess says, switching back to Belharan.
        
        "[pc.HeShe] and I — there are no secrets between us at this point. [pc.name] has saved our people from the complete and utter demonic corruption my sister was subject to. At this point, we need all the help we can get, and making sure [pc.heShe] understands the situation is paramount."
        
        "I'll speak, Regent. Not because you command it, but because [pc.name] made the effort to try and solve things peacefully between the two of us when we met. For someone like [pc.himHer], that's a lot of goodwill on [pc.hisHer] part where it wasn't warranted; I can at least appreciate that."

        "You." Hethia's voice is as dry as ever, unchanged from when you confronted her at Westbank over the fate of the loggers. The druidess eyes you up and down "Fancy seeing you here. I'd heard someone from outside of the Winter City happened to be declared the new Champion of Winter, but I didn't expect it to be you. Life is full of surprises, isn't it?"

        [var0
            |"Yes, [pc.himHer]. The three of us meet again, hopefully under more peaceable circumstances this time
            |Ryn purses her lips. "You know [pc.name]?"

            Hethia hesitates, then nods. "We were involved in an altercation over a disagreement recently. Instead of immediately taking arms, [pc.heShe] chose to hear me out and reach a peaceable resolution through negotiation. I... did not expect that from anyone who was not boer'alvar."
            
            That brings a warm, genuine smile to Ryn's face. "Well, how appropriate for what we're discussing today
        ]. Hethia, this is the recently enshrined Champion of Winter, instrumental in revealing my sister's corruption to all of the Winter City, and deposing her wickedness from the throne. I hope you'll give [pc.himHer] all the respect due to [pc.himHer] station."

        The druidess bites her lip and the warg at her side perks up its ears, but she nods. "I see. [pc.Name] has been fair to me as well."
        
        Ryn frowns and eyes you, trying her best to look contemplative and regal. "Well, that's a good start, if nothing else. How much do you know about the schism in the boer'alvar, [pc.name]?"
        
        Hethia told you some of it when you met her down at the logging camp, you remember. She had... less than glowing praise for the Winter City back then.
        
        The druidess swallows hard. "Let not mince words — that is the position that many of us exiles hold, and would still hold if not for recent developments."
        
        "Good, so I don't need to catch you up on that piece of history. On the other hand, these recent developments — for the sake of the Champion of Winter, Emissary, would you please enlighten my champion on those details?"
        
        Hethia winces. "I — Regent, this is — "
        
        At that, Ryn starts speaking to Hethia is what can only be their native tongue. The discussion is quite animated, if hushed, but Hethia eventually nods, even if she looks distinctly unhappy about it all.
        
        "It's fine to tell [pc.name] about it?" the druidess says, switching back to Belharan.
        
        "[pc.HeShe] and I — there are no secrets between us at this point. [pc.name] has saved our people from the complete and utter demonic corruption my sister was subject to. At this point, we need all the help we can get, and making sure [pc.heShe] understands the situation is paramount."
        
        "I'll speak, Regent. Not because you command it, but because [pc.name] made the effort to try and solve things peacefully between the two of us when we met. For someone like [pc.himHer], that's a lot of goodwill on [pc.hisHer] part where it wasn't warranted; I can at least appreciate that."

rows.original: "[pc.name]... our time is passing. The Old Wyld is fading, and much faster than any of us ever anticipated. When we exiled ourselves into the forests, we'd hoped to endure for generations, prove to the Winter City that we could still be strong and rebuild from our losses, show them the strength of our ways and beliefs. Our own weakness did us in. "Not just that, there are now foreigners in the Frostwood. They have drawn the spirits of the forests and fjords to them, have grown their own tree to rival ours. Every day, the land slips away from us, and becomes theirs. The power of the land that was once ours is slipping from our grasp and into theirs..." You see where this is going. Hethia looks away from you and Ryn and bites her lip; she's clearly struggling with herself. "We meant to last a thousand years, if not more, and have been reduced to this in merely two and a half centuries — the blink of an eye, comparatively speaking. Maybe... maybe the wyld trees — those that remain, anyway — are right. Maybe the time of the old spirits and powers is truly over." "Your own deities have given up?" "They are fading, and fast; the tree the foreigners have planted commands more and more of the Frostwood's soul every day, and our powers diminish proportionally. The Old Wyld is not sad about its passing; all things must die. Yet those of us who still follow it remain, and to these ends they have told us in no uncertain terms to stop being so stiff-necked and surrender. Once they can no longer protect us, our future will be in even deeper jeopardy. The wyld trees have determined... that it is best if we rejoin the Winter City and bridge the schism against the dark future they've foreseen." Uneasy silence hangs in the air. Now you see why Hethia is so conflicted — on one hand, her own deities whom she reveres have told her to throw herself onto the mercy of the royal family. On the other... the grudge the druids have against the var Ridell line and the Lumian priesthood, which is not wholly unjustified, runs deep, and the hatred burns like hot coals. The former may have won out, but it clearly hurts the druidess a lot to even be standing here discussing this with you; to say it's a bitter pill to swallow must be a great understatement. At last, it's Ryn who breaks the silence. "That's why Hethia came here to the Winter City, to negotiate terms with my sister, heal the schism in our people and end the druids' exile. It's a good thing that she came after we'd retaken the palace — I don't know what Alissa would have done to her." "At least part of the prophecies the wyld trees have given us is true. The queen of the Var Ridell line is now a demon, and a regent rules in her stead." Hethia shifts her gaze. "There are two main factions amongst us druids, but I think that the side arguing for reunification has had their arguments bolstered by these recent events in the Winter City. Darker times lie ahead for us as a people; we must not just stand together, but seek allies amongst other peoples as well." And so she's here to negotiate that return, or at least, begin the negotiations. You don't know all of this as deeply as a pale elf would, but it's obvious that this is a sticky situation with deep-seated hurts on both sides of the schism, even though they were not the ones who created them. In a way, that just makes the matter worse, as there's no one alive who can remember what things were like before the split... "That's quite right," Ryn replies. "And since they've shown goodwill in coming all the way here and showing their own weak hand up front, I think it's only fair that I reciprocate that and be magnanimous. [etheryn.lnhConfidence |If you, um, don't mind hearing me out? |I think I have an idea. |Well, I think I have a proposal for you, druidess. ]" "Regent." "All this will have to be done by degrees — the Winter City cannot accommodate all of you at once, not after the destruction the Godswar wrought on both the city itself and its people. The return of your people to the fold will take some time, and you on your part will need to readjust to living in the Winter City. We will need to expand the walls, build new homes for those who wish to live within, ensure that you all can be fed, made comfortable, and do useful work. While this is happening, you will be provided accommodations in the palace and stay on to oversee the reunification process and advise me as to the sensibilities of your — no, our people. Given that you're the best candidate for the task, druidess, it only makes sense. Will you accept?" "This... is a reasonable outcome, Regent." "I'm glad you think of it that way. rows.translation: "[pc.name]我们的时间正在流逝。古老的荒野正在迅速消逝，其速度远超我们所有人的预料。当初我们选择隐居在森林中，本希望能够世代延续下去，向冬城证明我们依然拥有力量，能够从失败中重新站起来，向他们展示我们的生活方式与信仰的力量。然而，正是我们自身的软弱导致了这一切。 不仅如此，现在弗罗斯特伍德里也出现了外国人。他们吸引了森林和峡湾中的精灵，还种下了属于自己的树木，这些树木甚至可以与我们的相媲美。每一天，这片曾经属于我们的土地都在一点点从我们手中溜走，变成了他们的……曾经属于我们的这片土地的力量，正在从我们手中消失，落入他们的手中…… 你应该能猜到这会走向何方。 赫希娅将目轻型从你和莱恩身上移开，咬住了嘴唇；显然，她正在与自己的内心作斗争。“我们原本以为自己能够存活一千年甚至更久，然而仅仅两个半世纪的时间，我们就落到了这样的地步——相对来说，这只不过是一眨眼而已。也许……也许那些野树——至少是那些还存活着的野树——是对的。也许那些古老的精灵和力量，真的已经结束了它们的时代。 你们自己的神明已经抛弃你们了吗？” “它们正在逐渐消失，而且速度越来越快；那些外国人种下的那棵树，每天都在吞噬越来越多的‘霜木’的灵魂，我们的力量也在随之减弱。 古老的荒野并不会为自身的消逝而悲伤；一切事物终究都会走向终结。然而，我们这些依然追随它的人们依然存在。为了我们的未来，它们已经明确地告诉我们：不要再固执己见了，必须屈服。一旦它们再无法保护我们，我们的命运将会陷入更加危险的境地。 那些古老的树木已经做出了决定……认为我们最好重新加入冬城，共同消除那些他们所预见的、将会带来暗影未来的分裂与矛盾。 空气中弥漫着令人不安的沉默。现在你应该明白为什么赫希娅会如此矛盾了吧——一方面，她所崇敬的神明告诉她，应该将自己的命运交托给王室；另一方面……德鲁伊们对里德尔家族以及卢米安神职人员的怨恨由来已久，这种怨恨并非毫无根据，它们如同灼热的炭火一般，始终在她心中燃烧着。 前者或许取得了胜利，但仅仅是因为要站在这里与你讨论这件事，就已经让这位德鲁伊女巫受到了极大的伤害；说这是一颗不得不吞下的苦药，简直还是轻描淡写了。 终于，是瑞恩打破了沉默。“这就是为什么赫希娅会来到冬城，与我妹妹谈判，试图弥合我们族群之间的分歧，结束德鲁伊们的流放生活。好在我们在夺回宫殿之后她才来到这里——否则我不知道艾莉莎会对她做出什么。 至少，那些野树给我们的预言有一部分是真实的。瓦瑞德尔家族的女王如今已经变成了恶魔，而一位摄政王正在代替她统治国家。”赫希娅转移了自己的视线，“在我们德鲁伊族群中，目前存在两大主要派系，但我认为，那些主张重新统一的人，他们的观点因为冬城最近发生的这些事件而得到了进一步的强化。对我们整个族群来说，更加暗影的时刻即将来临 必须 不仅要团结一致，还要在其他民族中寻找盟友。” 因此，她来到这里，就是为了协商这一回归事宜，或者至少开启谈判进程。你可能没有像苍白精灵那样深入了解这一切，但很明显，这是一个棘手的局面，分裂双方的伤痛都根深蒂固，尽管这些伤痛并非他们自己造成的。 从某种意义上说，这反而让事情变得更糟了，因为现在活着的人已经没有人能够记得分裂之前的情况是怎样的了…… “确实如此，”瑞恩回答道，“而且既然他们特意来到这里，还主动暴露了自己的弱点，我认为我理应以同样的方式回应他们，表现出宽容与大度。 [var0 |现在，赫希娅，我们在西岸相遇时，你或许对我有些冷淡，但为了和平的缘故，我愿意忽略你当时说过的话。这件事比我们个人之间的恩怨重要得多，我绝不会因为一次简单的侮辱就破坏和平谈判，从而证明自己不配担任摄政王。 当然，从瑞恩的说法来看 [etheryn.lnhConfidence |她所说的话完全是出于真心。赫希娅微笑着低下了头。 |这些话每一句都隐含着某种深意，在那些和解的言辞之下，其实隐藏着冷酷的锋芒。赫希娅微微一皱眉头，然后低下了头。 |每个人的言辞都冰冷而尖锐，就像冰柱的尖端；可以看出，尽管瑞恩愿意放下这件事，但它仍然在她心中留下了伤痛。赫希娅微微皱了皱眉，然后低下了头。 ] 当然。” “你觉得呢？ [pc.name]?"
