|嗯，我得回去处理一些事情，等处理完就会回来陪你们。” 她不是要留下来监督这次重新统一谈判吗？ “我本来是愿意的……但我想说，能和你们一起在外面待着，我会很开心的。 [pc.name]我并不羡慕埃尔萨拉所处的位置，但我相信她会为苍白精灵们做出最有利的事情，也不会让任何偏见影响她的决定。考虑到冬城发生的事情，我相信就连德鲁伊们也会理解，追捕卡希拉确实是摄政王的当务之急。 现在，请给我一点时间。” 说完，Ryn便转身朝门口走去，将你独自留在走廊里，让你不得不思考自己的选择……半个小时后，她才再次回来，点了点头，示意你可以继续跟她走了。 好吧， [pc.name]别担心，埃尔萨拉和赫希娅会尽他们所能合作的。” 嗯，如果她对他们如此信任，你又有什么资格质疑她的判断呢？那你该走了——今天你已经听够了那些政治上的废话了。 |好吧，我得回到王座厅去结束这次会面，把一些事情处理好。也许之后还会见到你，好吗？” 说完，瑞恩便朝门口走去，留下你独自在走廊里思考接下来的选择…… ]
rows.raw: " "[pc.name]... our time is passing. The Old Wyld is fading, and much faster than any of us ever anticipated. When we exiled ourselves into the forests, we'd hoped to endure for generations, prove to the Winter City that we could still be strong and rebuild from our losses, show them the strength of our ways and beliefs. Our own weakness did us in. "Not just that, there are now foreigners in the Frostwood. They have drawn the spirits of the forests and fjords to them, have grown their own tree to rival ours. Every day, the land slips away from us, and becomes theirs. The power of the land that was once ours is slipping from our grasp and into theirs..." You see where this is going. Hethia looks away from you and Ryn and bites her lip; she's clearly struggling with herself. "We meant to last a thousand years, if not more, and have been reduced to this in merely two and a half centuries — the blink of an eye, comparatively speaking. Maybe... maybe the wyld trees — those that remain, anyway — are right. Maybe the time of the old spirits and powers is truly over." "Your own deities have given up?" "They are fading, and fast; the tree the foreigners have planted commands more and more of the Frostwood's soul every day, and our powers diminish proportionally. The Old Wyld is not sad about its passing; all things must die. Yet those of us who still follow it remain, and to these ends they have told us in no uncertain terms to stop being so stiff-necked and surrender. Once they can no longer protect us, our future will be in even deeper jeopardy. The wyld trees have determined... that it is best if we rejoin the Winter City and bridge the schism against the dark future they've foreseen." Uneasy silence hangs in the air. Now you see why Hethia is so conflicted — on one hand, her own deities whom she reveres have told her to throw herself onto the mercy of the royal family. On the other... the grudge the druids have against the var Ridell line and the Lumian priesthood, which is not wholly unjustified, runs deep, and the hatred burns like hot coals. The former may have won out, but it clearly hurts the druidess a lot to even be standing here discussing this with you; to say it's a bitter pill to swallow must be a great understatement. At last, it's Ryn who breaks the silence. "That's why Hethia came here to the Winter City, to negotiate terms with my sister, heal the schism in our people and end the druids' exile. It's a good thing that she came after we'd retaken the palace — I don't know what Alissa would have done to her." "At least part of the prophecies the wyld trees have given us is true. The queen of the Var Ridell line is now a demon, and a regent rules in her stead." Hethia shifts her gaze. "There are two main factions amongst us druids, but I think that the side arguing for reunification has had their arguments bolstered by these recent events in the Winter City. Darker times lie ahead for us as a people; we must not just stand together, but seek allies amongst other peoples as well." And so she's here to negotiate that return, or at least, begin the negotiations. You don't know all of this as deeply as a pale elf would, but it's obvious that this is a sticky situation with deep-seated hurts on both sides of the schism, even though they were not the ones who created them. In a way, that just makes the matter worse, as there's no one alive who can remember what things were like before the split... "That's quite right," Ryn replies. "And since they've shown goodwill in coming all the way here and showing their own weak hand up front, I think it's only fair that I reciprocate that and be magnanimous. [var0 |Now, Hethia, you may have been curt with me when we met at Westbank, but in the interest of peace I'm willing to let the words you spoke back there slide. This is bigger than us, and I'm not about to show myself unworthy of being regent by scuttling peace talks over a simple insult." Of course, the way Ryn's saying it, [etheryn.lnhConfidence |She's being entirely genuine about her words. Hethia smiles, and bows her head. |There's just a bit of point in each and every one of them, cold steel under the reconciliatory words. Hethia winces, and bows her head. |Each one's sharp and cold, like the point of an icicle; you can tell that the whole matter still stings for Ryn, even if she's willing to let it go. Hethia winces, and bows her head. ] "Of course." "What do you think, [pc.name]?" [pc.isDK |Well, if it were just between the two of them and you were in her shoes, you wouldn't have let such a deep-cutting slight go just like that; a ruler also can't afford to show weakness in a situation like this. Then again, there's not much left of the pale elf court to scheme and intrigue, and there's also a delicious irony to the current situation of Hethia being more or less in Ryn's power and the latter just brushing off her insults back at Westbank like nothing. It's a very poignant scene, if you may say so. |Again, you're not exactly clear on the details of pale elf culture — if just letting go of a slight like what was given is taken as craven weakness, but from where you stand Ryn's certainly being the bigger woman by letting it go and showing that childish taunts like that don't bother her any. ] |We have to meet them halfway. But I'd like your counsel, [pc.name]." [pc.isDK |Well, if your opinion is being asked here, you're sure that Ryn's giving far more generous terms here than you'd have given. If it were up to you, you'd have demanded nothing less than complete and unconditional surrender, just to make a point. If you were a druid, you'd take Ryn's offer as-is — she's basically giving Hethia everything she wants, especially when the druids by all appearances are in a very poor bargaining position compared to the crown. |Well, if you're being asked for your opinion, Ryn's being very generous for being in a relative position of power in the negotiations; she's basically giving Hethia everything she wants, especially when the druids by all appearances are in a very poor bargaining position compared to the crown. You'd have expected both parties to hedge their bets before negotiating, but it looks like everyone just wants this to go as smoothly as possible, and that bodes well for the reunification. ] ] Ryn [etheryn.lnhConfidence |smiles weakly. "Thanks, [pc.name]. I needed to hear that." |grins. "Your counsel is appreciated, Champion of Winter." |grins. "Your counsel is appreciated, Champion of Winter." ] "Regent, if I may speak." Ryn nods at her high priestess. "Elthara?" "Regent, with all respect, I think you're being a little too magnanimous. When the druids exiled themselves from the Winter City, they swore to spill var Ridell blood for abandoning the Old Wyld. While I am sure that most druids desire reconciliation, there may be some... renegades who think otherwise." Well, if they wanted var Ridell blood, Alissa's has been spilled; certainly that should at least slake some of the thirst for revenge that the elven druids had. And let's be frank — given that Hethia's here in the Winter City trying to sue for peace, that they were the first ones to reach out instead of the other way around, you'd say that they've mellowed out a lot since then to want to extend the proverbial olive branch. Yes, there'll be those who still hold grudges, but then it's up to people like Hethia to police their own and keep them from sabotaging the reunification efforts. Ryn smiles at you. "[etheryn.lnhConfidence |Thanks, [pc.name]. You see, Elthara? People r-really can change |Thanks for speaking up, [pc.name]. It's great to know you've got my back |Thanks, [pc.name]. This is why I keep a champion like you around ]. But yes, Elthara, it may have been but two and a half centuries, but that isn't as short a time as we might imagine — if I learned anything after escaping from my sister's clutches, it's that our perception of time isn't the one that's relevant any more. Imagine my surprise when I spoke with the baroness of the Marches and discovered that not only was the treaty we had with them defunct, the backing authority had completely collapsed. And we will have to deal with other people going forward — we can't do this ourselves. If not for [pc.name], the Winter City would have been subverted from the inside by that demoness. We need friends and alliances, and this starts with our own." The high priestess of Lumia bows her head, but says nothing. "While traveling with [pc.name] and during my own explorations, I've had the opportunity to see some of the things the druids say are happening out in the Frostwood for myself, and they speak true. I can see how they are being subject to considerable pressure... and that has the potential to change people in a very short time. Out of necessity, if nothing else. "So, Elthara?" "I am satisfied, Regent. That being said, I do have one question for you, druidess. Does your renunciation of the Old Wyld mean that the schismatics will turn to the light of Lumia?" Something flickers behind Hethia's eyes — doubt, anger, exhaustion. She looks from Ryn, to you, then down to her warg by her side. "I don't know." Ryn thins her lips. "[etheryn.lnhConfidence |C-could you explain? |I'm not sure what you mean. |Come again? ]" "Just because the Wyld Trees have told us to turn away from them doesn't mean we'll bow before this human goddess of light from the south. Some of us may do so, in our own time and for our own reasons, but I won't speak for anyone else. Even with what has happened to Alissa, what with her banishment and all, some of the hardliners are not quite appeased, and would not have gone on if not for the direct command of the Wyld Trees. Asking us to convert all at once... may be a little too much to ask of us, too soon." "I think this is fair," Ryn replies with a nod. "Faith cannot be forced. Elthara, your own will not actively proselytize to them unasked, but if any of them wish to learn more about the light of Lumia, provide them with everything they need to set them upon the proper path. We will not insult their loss, and meet them halfway. [etheryn.lnhConfidence |If you, um, don't mind hearing me out? |I think I have an idea. |Well, I think I have a proposal for you, druidess. ]" "Regent." "All this will have to be done by degrees — the Winter City cannot accommodate all of you at once, not after the destruction the Godswar wrought on both the city itself and its people. The return of your people to the fold will take some time, and you on your part will need to readjust to living in the Winter City. We will need to expand the walls, build new homes for those who wish to live within, ensure that you all can be fed, made comfortable, and do useful work. While this is happening, you will be provided accommodations in the palace and stay on to oversee the reunification process and advise me as to the sensibilities of your — no, our people. Given that you're the best candidate for the task, druidess, it only makes sense. Will you accept?" "This... is a reasonable outcome, Regent." "I'm glad you think of it that way. No one's likely to get everything they want, but we're all trying to be reasonable and work towards the same goals here. Now, this audience is over — you may return to the other druids and inform them of the good news, then return to the palace and get settled in. Champion, a moment of your time, if you please — I would have words with you." Hmm? Your thoughts are cut short, though, as Ryn rises from her throne, takes you by the arm and [etheryn.lnhConfidence |nervously tugs you towards the door on the far end of the throne room that opens to the hallway to her private quarters. The moment it closes, the thin facade of bravery and confidence she had while speaking with Hethia collapses and she sags against you in relief. "Phew," Ryn says, heaving a sigh of relief. "T-that really took it out of me... it's hard, having to pretend throughout all of that." Heavy is the head that wears the crown — she already knew that, you suppose, but it's hard to imagine what it's like until you experience it for yourself. "Alissa made it all look so easy, but even she hated it. Although it was for different reasons, I guess. Thanks for being around for me, [pc.name] — half of the time I don't even know what I'm doing. Just having you around makes me think of what you might do, and I go with that; I know I'm not very good at anything so I shouldn't come up with my own ideas anyway because they're just bound to mess things up." |gently tugs you towards the door on the far end of the throne room that opens to the hallway to her private quarters.. Once the both of you are alone, her mask of calm fades and she heaves a small sigh. "Phew. That was tiring. I know I'm getting more and more used to this ruling business, but I feel like I'm treading on eggshells all the time and it really takes it out of me." Treading on eggshells is putting it lightly — like back there with Hethia, one wrong move would have jeopardised the entirety of the reunification process. Heavy is the head that wears the crown, as they say, but someone's got to make these decisions and better her than her sister calling the shots around here; even if she's less capable for now, she nevertheless has her own people in mind. Best a chance of failure than certain deliberate sabotage. "Alissa made it look all so easy — when she could bother with being royal, I guess..." From everything you've seen of her sister, she was plenty capable but disinclined to use her talents as they should have. That, as far as you're concerned, is worse than someone who's floundering but at least doing her best to improve and do the right thing. Ryn gives you a small smile. "T-thanks, [pc.name]. I really appreciate having you around at these times. When you backed me up... I felt like I was on even footing with Hethia there." |leads you out towards the door on the far end of the throne room leading to the private quarters, not looking back. The moment it closes behind the both of you, Ryn sighs, lets her shoulders sag and gives you a rueful smile. Long day, you take it? "Long enough. I've got so many people helping me, especially Elthara, and I'm really glad for you showing up back there when you did. Hethia's not even the worst encounter I've had by far ever since becoming Regent — at least she genuinely wants to work with me. Ruling is pretty exhausting." Heavy is the head that wears the crown — she already knew that, you suppose, but it's hard to imagine what it's like until you experience it for yourself. Ryn nods in agreement. "Alissa made it look all so easy — when she could be bothered to take on the mantle of royalty. I know I'm the better choice compared to her, but even so, there are some days where I wish I had her charisma. Even when she didn't know what she was doing, she always managed to appear as if she did." And look at where it led her. Alissa doesn't look like the type who would admit she would ever make a mistake, so naturally she ended up learning nothing. Ryn, on the other hand, can learn and grow. Ryn takes your hand in hers and gives it a squeeze. "Thanks, [pc.name]. It's nice to be reminded that I made the right choice in picking you as a champion. We were all walking on eggshells back there — even I knew what was at stake. And Elthara, although she's not a bad person, does have her blind spots when it comes to the druids, and the same thing goes in reverse. All in all... I know you didn't say that much, [pc.name], but thanks for showing up when you did and being there for me. It really means a lot." ] No problem. So, about Hethia... A sigh. "That's the first step there, I think. Like I said back there, the exact details of the druids' return will need to be hammered out in the coming days, and we'll certainly end up meeting them somewhere in the middle. The only question is how much one side's going to compromise with the other. From the reactions of otherwise good people like Elthara, it's going to be an uphill battle. "But Hethia's our best bet at this point. We'll have guest quarters prepared for her, and from there, arrange for audiences with the rest of her people with her present as a mediator. We intend to make the process quick as possible, after all. Given that the two of you have a good history, if you could visit her, predispose her to being more open-minded to our way of seeing things... I wouldn't mind, either." Well, that's something for you to work on. [party.has Etheryn |"Well, I'm going to go back in, tie up a few loose ends, and then I'll be back with you." She isn't going to stay, oversee the reunification talks? "I would... but I'm going to say I'll be glad to be out there with you, [pc.name]. I don't envy Elthara in her position, but I do trust her to do what's best for the pale elves and not let any of her prejudices come into play. I'm sure even the druids can understand that given what happened in the Winter City, hunting down Kasyrra is rightfully the Regent's top priority. Now, if you'll give me a moment." With that, Ryn's already heading back to the door, leaving you in the hallway to ponder your options... half an hour passes before she rejoins you with a nod. "All right, [pc.name]. Don't worry about it — Elthara and Hethia will cooperate as best as they can." Well, if she has so much trust in them, who are you to question her judgement? Time for you to be off, then — you've had enough political nonsense for a day. |"All right, I've got to be back in the throne room and finish up the audience, sort things out. Maybe I'll see you later, okay?" With that, Ryn's already heading back to the door, leaving you in the hallway to ponder your options... ] "

rows.original: "You!" The air in the room drops several degrees as Hethia's eyes meet yours and flash with fury. The druidess' lips part in a grimace-cum-snarl, her entire body tensing to spring like an animal caught in a trap. Her warg, previously lying down on the rug at her side, comes to attention and follows suit; every bit as willing to tear your throat out as it was back at Westbank. The tension in the room is stretch to breaking, the guards posted by the door and pillars are poised to leap into the fray; hurriedly, Ryn calms the situation by rising from her throne and gesturing downwards with both hands. [etheryn.lnhConfidence |"S-stop it! Both of you! I won't have a brawl in my throne room — explain yourselves!" |"That's enough out of the both of you!" Ryn's voice rings out over the throne room. There's not very much in the way of royal presence in her demeanour, but she's trying, at least. "I won't stand for petty fighting in my throne room — now simmer down and explain to me what's going on." |"Stop it! Both of you!" Ryn's voice rings out over the throne room. She's still got some ways to go when it comes to projecting a royal presence, but she's learning fast. "You two will remember where you are — I won't have this nonsense playing out before my presence. Now, explain to me what's going on and why the both of you look fit to come to blows." ] But of course. To make a long story short, you found Hethia Runasdottir here holding a group of loggers from Hawkethorne hostage in the wake of the blizzard back when all this began. She was being most unreasonable in her demands, especially in a forest which had become far more hostile in the wake of Kasyrra's passing, so you had no choice but to effect the loggers' release by taking her out of the equation. "No choice," the druidess spits. "You didn't even try to talk to me." Well, given the situation and how stuck-up she was being, everything you'd learned from Garret and the loggers she'd taken hostage — would she even have stood down and spoken peaceably with a [pc.race], let alone reached a satisfactory agreement? [etheryn.lnhConfidence |"P-please! Stop it! This isn't getting anywhere!" Despite her pleas, it's clear that Ryn isn't getting anywhere with defusing the situation — as it turns out, it's Elthara who steps in to save the day, waving off the palace guards who've begun closing in on the scene. "Champion, Emissary, you will maintain order before the regent here. I don't care what petty feuding you may have in your past; that's beyond the scope of these deliberations and should not color them. Champion, you know better than to place the regent's goals and well-being in jeopardy because of your spats; Emissary, the same goes for you when it comes to the situation of the druidic schismatics. Have a care for your duties and stop this nonsense right now." Ryn mops her brow. "Thank you, high priestess. But tell me, Emissary, what's your side of the story here?" |"Stop it, you two!" Raising her voice, Ryn does her best to look all regal and imperious — and given the pressure of the situation, actually succeeds. "I'm holding an audience, one of the first few since I became regent, and the both of you will maintain order before my throne. I don't care what petty feuding you may have in your past; that's beyond the scope of these deliberations and should not color them. Have a care for your duties and stop this nonsense right now." Ryn's words ring in the vast emptiness of the hall, and both Hethia and you share a sour glance before dropping it. Ryn mops her brow and settles back in her throne, tension still taut in her body. "All right. [pc.name], you've spoken your part — Tell me, Emissary, what's your side of the story here?" |"Enough, the both of you!" Raising her voice, Ryn sweeps her arms theatrically over the hall, the confidence of her royal presence radiating from her, cold and imperious as ice. "I'm holding an audience, one of the first few since I became regent, and the both of you will maintain order before my throne. I don't care what petty feuding you may have in your past; that's beyond the scope of these deliberations and should not color them. Have a care for your duties and stop this nonsense right now before I'm forced to ask the guards to break this up." Ryn's words in the throne room as she turns her gaze between the both of you, silence falling soon after. All that confidence you've tried to build in her is finally coming to the fore — if it weren't directed against you, you'd certainly be able to appreciate it better. As things stand, both Hethia and you share a sour glance before dropping the matter; satisfied, Ryn mops her brow and settles back in her throne, folding her hands on her lap. "All right. [pc.name], you've spoken your part — Tell me, Emissary, what's your side of the story here?" ] Hethia appears uncertain at that. "Regent, there are — " "I've named [pc.name] the Champion of Winter. [pc.HeShe] helped me depose my corrupt sister, and I trust [pc.himHer]. There are no secrets to be had here...now, speak." "The loggers were encroaching on one of the groves that housed one of the wyld trees, had taken to its outskirts with their axes. They needed to be stopped." Ryn steeples her fingers. "And you couldn't ask them to cease?" "The knowledge of the wyld trees' existence and other secrets of the Old Wyld are forbidden to those who are not boer'alvar." Hethia shoots you a glance. "Or at least to those who do not have express permission otherwise." A sigh. "I'm seeing how this ended up coming to blows." "Your champion also stole my whitewood bow after the fact." You couldn't quite leave it on her afterwards to come and be a threat while you were leading the loggers back to Hawkethorne, could you? Or do pale elves not disarm defeated opponents? But hey, that's enough from you — you've already derailed whatever this audience was about long enough. Now that introductions have been made, what's all this about, anyway? You gather it's some kind of diplomatic matter? Ryn leans forward in her throne and steeples her fingers. "How much do you know about the schism in the boer'alvar, [pc.name]?" Not much. Hethia certainly didn't say anything about it when you met her — no pale elf, Ryn herself included, has yet brought it up in detail. You can easily imagine it's one of those things which aren't spoken about to people outside the in-group. The druidess swallows hard at your jab. "Let's not mince words about the matter — it would take far too long to explain in sufficient clarity and detail. There are layers of contention, detail and nuance that would take forever to pick through." "That is true. On the other hand, these recent developments which you've just told me prior to my champion's arrival — for [pc.hisHer] sake, Emissary, would you please repeat yourself?" Hethia winces. "I — Regent, this is — " At that, Ryn starts speaking to Hethia is what can only be their native tongue. The discussion is quite animated, if hushed, but Hethia eventually nods, even if she looks distinctly unhappy about the prospect. "Then you will tell [pc.name] about it?" the druidess says, switching back to Belharan. "I consider it essential. That, and I repeat myself — there are no secrets between us at this point." Hethia sighs and squeezes her eyes shut, balls her fists and lets out a small but poignant sigh. When she's done, the druidess gives Ryn a long, slow nod. "I didn't expect this to be easy, but even so... I will do as the Old Wyld has commanded and swallow my pride."
rows.translation: 你！ 当赫希娅的目光与你的视线相遇时，房间里的空气仿佛骤然降了几度——她的双眼中闪烁着愤怒的光芒。这位德鲁伊的女子扭曲着嘴唇，发出一声既像咒骂又像咆哮的声音，整个身体都绷得紧紧的，仿佛是一只被困在陷阱里的野兽，随时准备扑上来攻击你。她身边的那头魔兽，之前正躺在地毯上，此刻也立刻警觉起来，同样准备扑向你；它和在西岸的时候一样，迫不及待地想要撕碎你的喉咙。 房间里的紧张气氛已经达到了令人窒息的程度，守在门口和柱子旁的卫兵们都随时准备冲进去干预。这时，瑞恩急忙从王座上站起来，用双手部向下示意，这才平息了局面的紧张气氛。 [etheryn.lnhConfidence |住口！你们两个！我可不允许在我的王座室里发生斗殴——快给我解释清楚！ |你们两个够了！”莱恩的声音在王座厅中回荡。她的举止中并没有太多王室成员该有的威严，但至少她是在努力表现出来。“我绝不允许在我的王座厅里发生这种无聊的争执——现在冷静下来，给我解释一下到底发生了什么。
