Sad, really |You'd seen them in the past — in fact, that kind overwhelmingly made up your clientele as a courtesan back in the day. The spare's spare of some local family or the other, lordlings and young ladies; kept around by their families as insurance for insurance, with not very much expected of them yet demanding all the luxuries of their station. They kept you in the black, but the attitude they invariably brought with them was insufferable |You'd seen them in the past — in fact, that kind overwhelmingly made up your clientele as a minstrel back in the day, playing at their parties and other social gatherings. The spare's spare of some local family or the other, lordlings and young ladies; kept around by their families as insurance for insurance, with not very much expected of them yet demanding all the luxuries of their station. Their patronage kept you in the black, but the attitude they invariably brought with them was insufferable — at least you weren't one of their whores, that would have been the pits |You'd always seen them in the past — pampered ponces going to and from their parties and social gatherings, feckless nobs of every stripe and color. A street rat like you was always beneath their notice, but that just made them all the better marks — and you never felt any kind of regret for cutting the purses of those insufferable prats on the streets ]. It isn't an exact analogy, but the stuck-up and know-it-all spirit is right on the money. "Hmph. Well, it seems like I'll be seeing a lot more of you around the palace, so there's always the possibility of our opinions of each other changing for the better. The regent likes you, and from everything I've heard you did do the boer'alvar a service by revealing the queen's corruption to the populace and saving us from being ruled by demons. That counts for something, I suppose. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a meeting with Elthara." With that, the druidess sweeps past you and strides off down the hallway, not looking back. [party.hasCompanions |[comp1.name] folds [comp1.hisHer] arms as [comp1.heShe] watches Hethia retreat. "Well, if she wasn't a nice person." Hmph, you agree. That's why you came to blow the first time around — negotiation wasn't on the table back at Westbank. Now, though, she'll be forced to play nice, and maybe that means you'll be able to get some words through. "A long shot, but if anyone can do it, it's you, [pc.name]. We'll just see what happens next, won't we?" Indeed. |Well, if she wasn't a nice person. You really couldn't have expected much better given how things went back at Westbank and in Ryn's audience chambers, but still if Hethia were more earnest about this whole peace process she could at least extend it to Ryn's champion, even if she doesn't hold anyone but those who were born pale elves in regard. Maybe... maybe being forced into a situation like this will encourage her to improve her outlook on other people. You can only hope. ] |Hethia gives you a curt nod as she sees you approaching her. "Champion of Winter." Please, [pc.name] will do. The druidess folds her arms. "Perhaps, but I need to get used to calling you by your title while also acknowledging the reality of someone not a boer'alvar being champion. Don't get me wrong — you've undoubtedly earned the right by aiding the regent in deposing her sister when so many others of their own people would, or could not help. No one is calling your strength into question... but still, it takes getting used to." You're appreciating the efforts that she's making to bridge the divide and change the attitudes of the druids. "As is Elthara from the other side. We all know this is necessary, every last one of us; it's just that some find it harder than most. The wounds are still fresh, and the heart doesn't necessarily follow the mind." How's she settling into the palace? She must find it quite unsettling, as a druid. "Not really." No? "When the boer'alvar walked in the Old Wyld, we used to have grand temples in the Frostwood. We still do, well-hidden and a little worse for the wear, but they either house the wyld trees, or are close to them. They are not too different from the palace of ice itself where it comes to architecture — the greenery is more confined, but much is still familiar. I'm not uncomfortable, and the regent has seen to it that I lack for nothing." You see. You'd imagined... well, something more natural, like she'd have slept in the boughs of a tree or something. Guess there's more you have to learn about her and her people, even given all that you know already. A rueful smile. "I think we're all clear on the fact that we've got a lot to work on in the future, Champion of Winter. Given the glacial pace boer'alvar proceedings usually proceed at from your perspective, a lot is being accomplished in a very short time. Now, is there some business you have with me?" ] ] "

rows.original: Ask Hethia about Xadaron Temple, or set off for it.
rows.translation: 可以向赫希娅询问关于萨达隆神庙的信息，或者直接前往那里。
rows.raw: "Ask Hethia about Xadaron Temple, or set off for it."

rows.original: Now that you're in a more relaxed setting with the druidess, maybe you can try and understand her better. [hethia.isHostile|As cold as she may affect to be, you still have to do your best, especially considering that she's the lead delegate to the Winter City from the druids.|You've been through a lot together, and yet you still don't know very much about what makes her tick; this is a great time to remedy that.]
rows.translation: 现在你和这位女德鲁伊处于一个更为轻松的环境中，或许你可以试着更好地理解她了。 [hethia.isHostile|尽管她表现得冷淡疏离，你仍然必须尽自己最大的努力，尤其是考虑到她是德鲁伊族派派往冬城的首席代表。|你们一起经历了许多事情，然而你仍然对她的内心世界知之甚少；现在正是弥补这一缺点的绝佳时机。]
rows.raw: "Now that you're in a more relaxed setting with the druidess, maybe you can try and understand her better. [hethia.isHostile|As cold as she may affect to be, you still have to do your best, especially considering that she's the lead delegate to the Winter City from the druids.|You've been through a lot together, and yet you still don't know very much about what makes her tick; this is a great time to remedy that.]"

rows.original: Return Hethia her bow as a peace offering. You're not expecting it to fully heal all wounds, but at least it'd be a good step towards repairing relations with the druidess.
rows.translation: 把赫希娅的弓还给她，作为和平的象征。你不能指望这把弓能治愈所有的伤痛，但至少这是修复与这位德鲁伊女士关系的良好开端。
rows.raw: "Return Hethia her bow as a peace offering. You're not expecting it to fully heal all wounds, but at least it'd be a good step towards repairing relations with the druidess."

rows.original: Naturally, you must have Hethia's bow on you to be able to return it to her. If you sold it or threw it away, well, you're out of luck, aren't you?
rows.translation: 当然，你必须带着赫希娅的弓才能把它还给她。如果你把它卖掉了或者扔掉了，那么你就运气不好了，对吧？
rows.raw: "Naturally, you must have Hethia's bow on you to be able to return it to her. If you sold it or threw it away, well, you're out of luck, aren't you?"

rows.original: Perhaps she could tell her something about herself?
rows.translation: 或许她可以告诉自己一些关于她自己的事情吧？
rows.raw: "Perhaps she could tell her something about herself?"

rows.original: How's staying in the palace treating her while she leads her side in the reunification talks? You hope that Ryn's being a good host.
rows.translation: 她在宫中生活得怎么样？同时，她还在负责领导自己的阵营参与统一谈判。你希望瑞恩能尽到一个好主人的责任吧。
rows.raw: "How's staying in the palace treating her while she leads her side in the reunification talks? You hope that Ryn's being a good host."

rows.original: [flags.XADARON_TS|Things are looking up for her people, aren't they?|This is at the crux of everything that's happened — why she was at Westbank, why she's here now. Understanding the beliefs of the pale elf druids in a deeper sense would hopefully help you connect with Hethia...]
rows.translation: [flags.XADARON_TS|她的人们的情况正在好转，不是吗？|这正是所有事情的核心所在——为什么她会出现在西岸，为什么现在会在这里。如果能够更深入地理解那些苍白精灵德鲁伊的信仰，或许就能帮助你与赫希娅建立联系……]
rows.raw: "[flags.XADARON_TS|Things are looking up for her people, aren't they?|This is at the crux of everything that's happened — why she was at Westbank, why she's here now. Understanding the beliefs of the pale elf druids in a deeper sense would hopefully help you connect with Hethia...] "

rows.original: Inquire about the day Ryn's dad, the king dowager, died.
rows.translation: 询问莱恩的父亲——王太后去世的具体日期。
rows.raw: "Inquire about the day Ryn's dad, the king dowager, died."

rows.original: [hethia.isHostile |Hethia scowls. "Are you in the habit of asking just anyone for their complete life stories, Champion of Winter? To bare their naked soul to you for your entertainment?" Actually, no. Only mostly when you're trying to get to know them better and understand their point of view. The scowl deepens. "I didn't expect you to answer that seriously." Oh, you got her sarcasm just fine, it's just that you thought a direct and honest answer would be more constructive here than spiralling into spite. Ryn did order you to play nice, after all. "Yeah, whatever. Maybe you should've done that whole talking thing the first time we met, but you've already shown yourself to be someone who's more than happy to draw arms first and ask questions later. I don't know if you're genuinely interested or not, and frankly, I don't care — I don't feel like discussing myself with you in the slightest." But Ryn — "Told us to be professional, and this is digging a little too deeply to be considered professional by any stretch of the imagination. No, I will not tell you about cute little anecdotes about myself that are irrelevant to the situation at hand, and this is well within my means, getting to know each other better notwithstanding. I'm sure that you've gained a lot of insight into me from this exchange, so there you have it." You sigh. This is going to be a little harder than you imagine it might be. Hethia's current hostile disposition towards you means that she's not inclined to make small talk about herself to you. Finding some way to improve her attitude would be for the best given all parties involved. |[rand |"I hadn't even been born when the schism happened and the rift opened between the boer'alvar as a people — a girl, I was initiated into the druidic circles as soon as I was old enough. The Winter City was only something you heard of from other people, or at best a bastion of an enemy to be gazed on by afar." By your reckoning, she's fairly young for a pale elf. Older than Ryn, maybe about the same as Alissa... but that only highlights how unprepared for rulership the former must be, and at least explains some of the fecklessness of the latter in throwing in with Kas. Gods, since Ryn's parents passed away the pale elves have been governed by people who're effectively children, but at least Ryn's doing her best and taking this seriously, which is more than what can be said for her sister. But back to the point... "You're not wrong. I still am very young — it is true that I'm a grower of the first circle, but my advancement is less because of any true merit on my part and needing to fill the shoes of those who've died in so short a time." Hethia gives you a rueful smile. "I believe that you people have an adage about not asking a woman her age, but given the circumstances I don't think that that applies here any more." Thirty? Forty? Maybe fifty? You know pale elves expect to live about two hundred years. What would young be in that context? "Close enough. I... I remember the tales I was told about the day when the druids decided to leave the Winter City, that the Queen had turned apostate from the Old Wyld and we were going into exile. I... I still have family within the walls of the Winter City, removed as we are." Has she been to see them? "I tried. But... it's as if I were talking to strangers, [pc.name]. My kin were certainly cordial enough, were glad to see me as a long-lost relative and happy that we'd all made it through the Godswar relatively unscathed. But no matter how I put it, they just weren't people I could easily think of as kin, and neither was I to them. Too much had changed, and we all knew that." That doesn't mean anything. If things changed in the two and a half centuries that they were apart, then they can continue to change — and for the better, too. You all... you all just have to believe in Ryn and her convictions. |Has she been a druid long? "I was initiated as a girl, so I've been one almost all my life. The training starts very young, where promising children — out of the few we still manage to have — are picked for further development, and finally initiation. The custom was to wait until sixteen, but because of circumstances since the Godswar that was pushed back to twelve. Even though there was a reduced need for us amongst the schismatic exiles, far, far too many had died during the Godswar or even worse, lost their powers when the wyld trees they served withered and died from the fungal blight the wraiths' servants concocted. They could pass on their knowledge, but could no longer put it into practice." So, this is all that she's ever known. "It's not a bad existence, [pc.name]. It gives me the opportunity to come into conflict, to fight, and I've been told that I enjoy it just a little too much." Fighting's not bad in and of itself... but she does need to have a good cause to fight for. "Which thanks to you, the wyld trees and the regent alike, I have." A smile. "I have no regrets being born just in time, at a place poised to have a hand in shaping the future of the boer'alvar. To be sure, it's hard, but few things worth doing are ever easy." |Has she considered what she's going to be doing after all this is done? "What do you mean?" Well, from where you're standing it looks like there isn't going to be much calling for druids in the future. Not just because of the wyld trees slowly passing, but also because the space that they used to occupy in pale elf society has been filled while they were gone. Sure, it's not going to happen all at once, but it's best to consider these issues well ahead of time. No doubt they're part of the talks — what role the returned schismatics will play after reunification — but you want to hear what she herself has in mind for her future. "I know what I want isn't likely to be what I'm going to get..." Yes, but you're still asking her anyway. Hethia gives you a faint smile. "Well, if we're making wishes, I'd wish to end up as a vinter. Find myself some nice land on which to grow berries and make the good stuff — I always envied the few remaining vintners we had even while I was being trained for more serious duties. Luxuries were in short supply... the few who were dedicated to wine-making understood it was only so that the knowledge wouldn't be forgotten. I'd wish to put it back into practice on a larger scale." It beats diplomatic work, doesn't it? "Oh, don't get me wrong — I do get a little thrill out of having screaming matches with Elthara without doing any screaming; it makes one feel good and gets the blood pumping. But like I said, if we're talking about wishing... yes, I'd like to be a vinter when this is all over. No doubt the regent would like to keep me on as some kind of advisor or special counsel on matters pertaining to us exiles for some time, but a woman can dream, can't she?" Well, maybe she can do it as a hobby; you're sure Ryn would be willing to indulge her whims if things go well for everyone and the reunification is smooth. "Ha! That's as much as I can hope for." |"Norathar and I were introduced to each other not long after I'd been initiated," Hethia says. "A bitch had recently whelped, and since the circle saw much traveling in my future they saw fit to present me with one of the warg pups and see if we were a good match for each other. Happily, we were." You know the pale elves ride wargs — does she ride her companion often? "Norathar carries me from place to place when need be. No doubt the palace guards ride the beasts in their kennels, but I don't use Norathar as a mount. There's a small but important difference there." Did that change in approach happen before or after the schism? "After, I'd wager. Before we druids left pale elf society, we used to raise all the wargs for use by the rest of the boer'alvar, but since our departure the palace of ice has seen fit to establish kennels of its own. I can't say that the animals they use aren't effectively trained — they're based on our own methods, after all — but there's something lacking in the poor beasts that my Norathar isn't short of." Pride? "That too, but it's not what I meant. It's hard to put into words — the wargs in the kennels aren't subjugated, but it's more like they've locked themselves into cages of their own making. I tried communicating with them and they were responsive and happy enough, but they just didn't see things the way Norathar did. "And I'd like to think that the difference was caused by the way Norathar and I treat each other, which certainly is fundamentally different from how the palace guards treat theirs." You'd say it's just the obvious result of the different ways the two sides of the pale elves see the world, and that's filtered down to even their animals. "If you see it that way. Me, I still think my Norathar is the best just as she is now." |If Hethia hadn't been a druidess... what would she have been? What is — no, was — life as a schismatic like? Hethia frowns. "It's hard for me to imagine myself as anything but a druid..." It's true that her profession has shaped her life from a very young age, and no doubt she wouldn't be the woman she is today otherwise. Still, you'd like her to entertain you, if only to learn more about the other half of the pale elves as a people. "Well, those who don't make the cut as druids for some reason or the other nevertheless have good prospects. Vintners were one avenue that I'd have liked to have been able to pursue, even if there wasn't much call for them. Working in the kennels, maybe masonry to try and keep the temples from crumbling in on themselves... "I'd have liked to have some more conflict, some more excitement in my life than that, though. Maybe hunting, although if I had taken up that mantle I'd probably have overhunted the woods something fierce." You laugh. Someone like Hethia? Sure, you could've seen her doing that. Her whitewood bow would've served her well in that line of work. "If I'd taken up that line of work, I wouldn't have had it." Ah, of course... "Such prestige the druids used to have that even the rejects were well-regarded. I can only wonder what it must've been like before the schism... but there's no point considering it now, is there? It's for those scraps of regard the stiff-necked on my side are still clinging to — after the reunification, they'll lose even that. Me, I just think it's a good blank slate to build upon — do-overs are exceedingly rare in this world." ] ]
rows.translation: [hethia.isHostile |赫希娅皱起了眉头：“冬之冠军，你是不是有什么习惯，就是随便找谁就询问他们完整的人生经历？就为了让自己获得娱乐吗？” 其实并不是这样。大多数情况下，我只是想更好地了解他们，理解他们的观点而已。 他的眉头皱得更深了。“我没想到你会认真回答那个问题。” 哦，你完全理解了她那句讽刺的话，只是你认为，在这里，直接而诚实的回答反而会比陷入怨恨更有意义吧。 毕竟，Ryn确实是命令你要有礼貌的。 “是啊，随便吧。也许在我们第一次见面的时候你就应该直接这么说了，但事实证明，你其实更喜欢先动手解决问题，然后再去问问题。 我不知道你是不是真的感兴趣，说实话，我也不在乎——我根本没兴趣和你讨论关于我自己的事情。” 但是，Ryn…… “你让我们保持专业，可现在的讨论已经深入到连专业都算不上的地步了。 不，我会的。 不是 我会讲一些与当前话题无关的、关于我自己的有趣小故事，这样做完全不在我的能力范围之内，不过这确实有助于我们更好地了解彼此。我相信，通过这次交流，你们一定已经对我有了很多了解，就是这样吧。 你叹了口气。看来这会比你想象的要困难一些。 目前，赫希娅对你怀有敌意，这意味着她并不愿意与你闲聊关于她自己的事情。考虑到所有相关方的利益，找到某种方法来改善她的态度才是最明智的做法。 |[rand |当那场分裂发生，布尔人这个民族出现裂痕时，我甚至还没有出生。作为一个女孩，等我长大到一定年龄后，就被接纳进了德鲁伊的圈子。对于冬城，人们最多只是从别人口中听说过，或者认为它不过是敌人的一座堡垒，远远地望着罢了。按照你的说法，对于一个苍白精灵来说，她确实还算比较年轻。她比瑞恩年长一些，或许和艾丽莎差不多大……但这也恰恰说明，前者在担任统治者方面肯定缺乏准备，而后者之所以会轻易加入卡斯的阵营，至少也可以用这一点来解释她的轻率行为。 天啊，自从瑞恩的父母去世后，这些苍白精灵实际上就一直由一些并不称职的人来统治着。 孩子们不过至少瑞恩正在尽她最大的努力，并且认真对待这件事，这已经比她姐姐做得好了。 不过，还是回到正题吧…… “你说得没错。我确实还很年轻—— 是 确实，我属于第一圈的修炼者，但我的进步之所以缓慢，并非因为我有什么特别的才能，而是因为我需要在如此短的时间内接替那些已经去世的人的位置。”赫希娅露出了一丝遗憾的笑容，“我想你们应该有这样一句俗语：不要问一个女人的年龄……但考虑到目前的处境，我认为这条俗语已经不再适用了。三十岁？四十岁？也许五十岁吧？你知道，淡色精灵的平均寿命大约有两百年。在这种标准下，三十岁还算很年轻吧？ “差不多吧。我……我记得那些关于德鲁伊们决定离开冬城的传说，据说女王背叛了古老的森林之神，所以我们都将被迫流亡。 我……我的家人仍然住在冬城里，只是我们被分开了。 她去见过他们吗？ “我试过了。但是……感觉就像是在和陌生人说话一样。 [pc.name]我的亲人们确实非常热情，他们把我当作久别重逢的亲人来欢迎，也很高兴我们都能在神战之中安然无恙地活下来。但无论如何，我总觉得他们并不是真正意义上的亲人，对他们来说，我也一样。 变化实在太大，我们所有人也都清楚这一点。 但这并不意味着什么。如果在他们分开的这两个半世纪里情况发生了变化，那么这些变化还会继续下去——而且很可能会变得更好。 你们所有人……都必须相信瑞恩以及她的信念。 |她当德鲁伊已经很久了吗？ “我小时候就被接纳为德鲁伊，所以几乎我的整个人生都在从事这个职业。训练从很小的时候就开始了，那些被认定有潜力的孩子——在我们还能找到的为数不多的这类孩子中——会被选中接受进一步的培养，最终正式成为德鲁伊。 按照惯例，这个年龄应该是十六岁，但由于“神战”带来的种种影响，这个年龄被提前到了十二岁。虽然在那些分裂出来的流亡者中，我们对他们的需求已经减少了，但在“神战”期间，还是有太多人失去了生命；更糟糕的是，那些他们所侍奉的野生树木因为怨灵的仆从们制造的真菌疫病而枯萎死亡，导致他们也失去了自己的力量。 他们能够将自己的知识传授下去，但却再也无法将其付诸实践了。” 所以，这就是她所熟知的一切。 “这样的生活也并非坏事。 [pc.name]这让我有机会陷入冲突、参与战斗，而且有人告诉我，我其实太享受这种过程了。” 战斗本身并没有什么坏处……但前提是她必须有为之战斗的正当理由。 多亏了你，还有那些野生树木以及那位统治者，我才能拥有这一切。”他微笑着说道，“能够恰好在这个时刻出生，在一个能够为‘布尔阿尔瓦’的未来发展做出贡献的地方出生，我毫不后悔。当然，这很艰难，但任何值得去做的事情，从来都不会是一帆风顺的。" |她有没有考虑过，当这一切结束后，自己该做什么？ “你是什么意思？” 嗯，从你的角度来看，未来似乎不会再有多少人需要德鲁伊了。 这不仅仅是因为那些野生树木正在逐渐消失，更因为在它们消失的过程中，它们在苍白精灵社会中曾经占据的位置已经被其他人或事物所占据。当然，这一切不会一下子发生，但最好还是提前认真考虑这些问题。 毫无疑问，这些话题肯定也在讨论之中——比如那些分裂出去的人在重新统一后将会扮演什么样的角色——但你真正想听到的，其实是另外一些事情。 她 她自己心中所考虑的是 她 未来。 “我知道我想要的，很可能并不是我最终能得到的……” 是的，但你还是还是要去问她。 赫希娅对你露出了一丝淡淡的微笑：“嗯，既然我们要许愿的话，我希望自己能成为一名冬日使者。 我得找一块合适的土地，在那里种植浆果，制作那些美味的饮品——即使在接受更重要的职责培训时，我也一直羡慕那些仍在从事葡萄酒酿造工作的少数人。奢侈品实在是非常稀缺……那些致力于葡萄酒制作的人明白，只有这样，这些知识才不会被遗忘。 我希望能在一个更大的规模上将其付诸实践。 这总比搞外交手段要简单吧？ “哦，别误会我的意思——和埃尔萨拉争吵虽然不会真的大喊大叫，但那种争执过程确实会让我感到兴奋；这种感觉很棒，能让人的血液加速流动。不过，就像我之前说的，如果我们要谈论未来的愿望的话……没错，等这一切结束后，我真希望能成为一名‘冬人’。毫无疑问，摄政王会希望我继续担任某种顾问或者特别代表，负责处理与我们这些流亡者相关的事宜，但女人总可以怀有一些梦想吧，不是吗？ 嗯，也许她可以把这当作一种爱好来做；如果你们的计划都能顺利实施，重聚也能顺利进行的话，我相信Ryn一定会愿意满足她的这个愿望的。 “哈！这已经是我能期望的全部了。 |在我加入那个组织不久之后，我和诺拉塔尔就被介绍认识了，”赫希娅说道。“当时有一只母狼刚刚生了幼崽，而由于他们预见我未来需要经常四处奔波，所以他们认为让我和其中一只幼崽在一起相处，看看我们是否合得来，是个不错的主意。幸运的是，我们确实很合得来。” 你知道那些苍白精灵会骑着狼兽出行——她经常骑着她的伙伴出行吗？ “诺拉塔尔 携带 在需要时，我会在不同的地方之间移动。毫无疑问，宫廷卫兵会骑着他们饲养的野兽出行，但我并不会使用诺拉塔尔作为坐骑。这两者之间存在着微小却重要的区别。 这种行事方式上的变化，是发生在分裂之前，还是之后呢？ 当然是在那之后。在我们德鲁伊离开苍白精灵的社会之前，我们一直都是负责饲养那些狼人，以便其他博尔阿尔瓦族人使用。但自从我们离开后，冰之宫殿就开始自己建立饲养场来饲养这些动物了。我不能说他们饲养的动物训练得不好——毕竟这些方法还是借鉴了我们的——不过那些可怜的家伙们似乎缺少了某些东西，而我的诺拉塔尔族人却并不缺乏这些东西。骄傲吗？” “也是，但那并不是我想要表达的意思。这种感觉很难用语言来描述——那些被关在狗舍里的狼 被征服的但事实上，他们更像是把自己关在了自己制造的笼子里。我尝试与他们沟通，他们也回应得很好，看起来也很开心，只不过他们看待事物的方式与诺拉塔尔不同而已。 我认为，这种差异之所以存在，是因为诺拉塔尔和我对待彼此的方式截然不同——这种差异显然与宫廷卫兵对待他们宠物的方式有着本质上的区别。” 有人可能会说，这只是苍白精灵这两个派系看待世界的方式不同所导致的必然结果，而这种差异甚至影响到了他们所饲养的动物。 如果你这么看的话……不过我觉得，我的诺拉瑟尔，就目前这个样子，已经是最完美的了。 |如果赫希娅不是德鲁伊……她会是什么呢？作为这样的异端者，生活到底是怎样的呢？ 赫希娅皱起了眉头：“我很难想象自己会成为除了德鲁伊之外的任何身份…… 的确，她的职业从她很小的时候起就塑造了她的人生，如果没有这份职业，她肯定不会成为今天的她。不过，人们还是希望她能为大家带来娱乐，至少这样就能更多地了解这些苍白精灵这个族群的另一面。 嗯，那些因为种种原因无法成为德鲁伊的人，其实也有其他不错的发展前景。酿酒师这个职业就是我曾经想要尝试的方向，尽管当时对这类人才的需求并不是很大。 在犬舍里工作，或许还需要做一些砌筑工作，以防止那些庙宇的结构发生坍塌…… “不过，我其实希望自己的生活中能有一些更多的冲突，一些更多的刺激元素。 也许可以尝试打猎，不过如果我 拥有过 如果我接下了那个任务，恐怕会在森林里过度狩猎，把那里的动物都猎杀殆尽。” 你笑了。像赫希娅这样的人吗？当然，你可以想象她会那么做。她的白木弓在这种工作中肯定能派上大用场。 如果我选择了那条职业道路，我就不会遇到这样的麻烦了。” 啊，当然…… “德鲁伊们曾经拥有如此高的声望，以至于那些被排斥在外的人也受到人们的尊重。我真想知道，在分裂之前，他们的地位该是怎样的。…但现在考虑这些也已经没有意义了，对吧？那些顽固的人还在坚持着那些微不足道的执念——等到重新统一之后，他们甚至连这些也会失去的。而我，只是认为这是一个可以重新开始的好机会罢了——在这个世界上，重新来过的机会实在是太罕见了。" ] ]
rows.raw: " [hethia.isHostile |Hethia scowls. "Are you in the habit of asking just anyone for their complete life stories, Champion of Winter? To bare their naked soul to you for your entertainment?" Actually, no. Only mostly when you're trying to get to know them better and understand their point of view. The scowl deepens. "I didn't expect you to answer that seriously." Oh, you got her sarcasm just fine, it's just that you thought a direct and honest answer would be more constructive here than spiralling into spite. Ryn did order you to play nice, after all. "Yeah, whatever. Maybe you should've done that whole talking thing the first time we met, but you've already shown yourself to be someone who's more than happy to draw arms first and ask questions later. I don't know if you're genuinely interested or not, and frankly, I don't care — I don't feel like discussing myself with you in the slightest." But Ryn — "Told us to be professional, and this is digging a little too deeply to be considered professional by any stretch of the imagination. No, I will not tell you about cute little anecdotes about myself that are irrelevant to the situation at hand, and this is well within my means, getting to know each other better notwithstanding. I'm sure that you've gained a lot of insight into me from this exchange, so there you have it." You sigh. This is going to be a little harder than you imagine it might be. Hethia's current hostile disposition towards you means that she's not inclined to make small talk about herself to you. Finding some way to improve her attitude would be for the best given all parties involved. |[rand |"I hadn't even been born when the schism happened and the rift opened between the boer'alvar as a people — a girl, I was initiated into the druidic circles as soon as I was old enough. The Winter City was only something you heard of from other people, or at best a bastion of an enemy to be gazed on by afar." By your reckoning, she's fairly young for a pale elf. Older than Ryn, maybe about the same as Alissa... but that only highlights how unprepared for rulership the former must be, and at least explains some of the fecklessness of the latter in throwing in with Kas. Gods, since Ryn's parents passed away the pale elves have been governed by people who're effectively children, but at least Ryn's doing her best and taking this seriously, which is more than what can be said for her sister. But back to the point... "You're not wrong. I still am very young — it is true that I'm a grower of the first circle, but my advancement is less because of any true merit on my part and needing to fill the shoes of those who've died in so short a time." Hethia gives you a rueful smile. "I believe that you people have an adage about not asking a woman her age, but given the circumstances I don't think that that applies here any more." Thirty? Forty? Maybe fifty? You know pale elves expect to live about two hundred years. What would young be in that context? "Close enough. I... I remember the tales I was told about the day when the druids decided to leave the Winter City, that the Queen had turned apostate from the Old Wyld and we were going into exile. I... I still have family within the walls of the Winter City, removed as we are." Has she been to see them? "I tried. But... it's as if I were talking to strangers, [pc.name]. My kin were certainly cordial enough, were glad to see me as a long-lost relative and happy that we'd all made it through the Godswar relatively unscathed. But no matter how I put it, they just weren't people I could easily think of as kin, and neither was I to them. Too much had changed, and we all knew that." That doesn't mean anything. If things changed in the two and a half centuries that they were apart, then they can continue to change — and for the better, too. You all... you all just have to believe in Ryn and her convictions. |Has she been a druid long? "I was initiated as a girl, so I've been one almost all my life. The training starts very young, where promising children — out of the few we still manage to have — are picked for further development, and finally initiation. The custom was to wait until sixteen, but because of circumstances since the Godswar that was pushed back to twelve. Even though there was a reduced need for us amongst the schismatic exiles, far, far too many had died during the Godswar or even worse, lost their powers when the wyld trees they served withered and died from the fungal blight the wraiths' servants concocted. They could pass on their knowledge, but could no longer put it into practice." So, this is all that she's ever known. "It's not a bad existence, [pc.name]. It gives me the opportunity to come into conflict, to fight, and I've been told that I enjoy it just a little too much." Fighting's not bad in and of itself... but she does need to have a good cause to fight for. "Which thanks to you, the wyld trees and the regent alike, I have." A smile. "I have no regrets being born just in time, at a place poised to have a hand in shaping the future of the boer'alvar. To be sure, it's hard, but few things worth doing are ever easy." |Has she considered what she's going to be doing after all this is done? "What do you mean?" Well, from where you're standing it looks like there isn't going to be much calling for druids in the future. Not just because of the wyld trees slowly passing, but also because the space that they used to occupy in pale elf society has been filled while they were gone. Sure, it's not going to happen all at once, but it's best to consider these issues well ahead of time. No doubt they're part of the talks — what role the returned schismatics will play after reunification — but you want to hear what she herself has in mind for her future. "I know what I want isn't likely to be what I'm going to get..." Yes, but you're still asking her anyway. Hethia gives you a faint smile. "Well, if we're making wishes, I'd wish to end up as a vinter. Find myself some nice land on which to grow berries and make the good stuff — I always envied the few remaining vintners we had even while I was being trained for more serious duties. Luxuries were in short supply... the few who were dedicated to wine-making understood it was only so that the knowledge wouldn't be forgotten. I'd wish to put it back into practice on a larger scale." It beats diplomatic work, doesn't it? "Oh, don't get me wrong — I do get a little thrill out of having screaming matches with Elthara without doing any screaming; it makes one feel good and gets the blood pumping. But like I said, if we're talking about wishing... yes, I'd like to be a vinter when this is all over. No doubt the regent would like to keep me on as some kind of advisor or special counsel on matters pertaining to us exiles for some time, but a woman can dream, can't she?" Well, maybe she can do it as a hobby; you're sure Ryn would be willing to indulge her whims if things go well for everyone and the reunification is smooth. "Ha! That's as much as I can hope for." |"Norathar and I were introduced to each other not long after I'd been initiated," Hethia says. "A bitch had recently whelped, and since the circle saw much traveling in my future they saw fit to present me with one of the warg pups and see if we were a good match for each other. Happily, we were." You know the pale elves ride wargs — does she ride her companion often? "Norathar carries me from place to place when need be. No doubt the palace guards ride the beasts in their kennels, but I don't use Norathar as a mount. There's a small but important difference there." Did that change in approach happen before or after the schism? "After, I'd wager. Before we druids left pale elf society, we used to raise all the wargs for use by the rest of the boer'alvar, but since our departure the palace of ice has seen fit to establish kennels of its own. I can't say that the animals they use aren't effectively trained — they're based on our own methods, after all — but there's something lacking in the poor beasts that my Norathar isn't short of." Pride? "That too, but it's not what I meant. It's hard to put into words — the wargs in the kennels aren't subjugated, but it's more like they've locked themselves into cages of their own making. I tried communicating with them and they were responsive and happy enough, but they just didn't see things the way Norathar did. "And I'd like to think that the difference was caused by the way Norathar and I treat each other, which certainly is fundamentally different from how the palace guards treat theirs." You'd say it's just the obvious result of the different ways the two sides of the pale elves see the world, and that's filtered down to even their animals. "If you see it that way. Me, I still think my Norathar is the best just as she is now." |If Hethia hadn't been a druidess... what would she have been? What is — no, was — life as a schismatic like? Hethia frowns. "It's hard for me to imagine myself as anything but a druid..." It's true that her profession has shaped her life from a very young age, and no doubt she wouldn't be the woman she is today otherwise. Still, you'd like her to entertain you, if only to learn more about the other half of the pale elves as a people. "Well, those who don't make the cut as druids for some reason or the other nevertheless have good prospects. Vintners were one avenue that I'd have liked to have been able to pursue, even if there wasn't much call for them. Working in the kennels, maybe masonry to try and keep the temples from crumbling in on themselves... "I'd have liked to have some more conflict, some more excitement in my life than that, though. Maybe hunting, although if I had taken up that mantle I'd probably have overhunted the woods something fierce." You laugh. Someone like Hethia? Sure, you could've seen her doing that. Her whitewood bow would've served her well in that line of work. "If I'd taken up that line of work, I wouldn't have had it." Ah, of course... "Such prestige the druids used to have that even the rejects were well-regarded. I can only wonder what it must've been like before the schism... but there's no point considering it now, is there? It's for those scraps of regard the stiff-necked on my side are still clinging to — after the reunification, they'll lose even that. Me, I just think it's a good blank slate to build upon — do-overs are exceedingly rare in this world." ] ] "

rows.original: [hethia.isHostile |[rand |"Hmph, it's sufficient. The regent herself is very accommodating, but it's plain as day that she's new at this whole diplomacy thing if she thinks to furnish delegates to her standards and not theirs. Not that she would be expected to know, but others won't be as understanding as I am when they're looking to find fault with her over the smallest things." What's the matter? As you understand it, Hethia's been given the best the palace of ice has to afford. Board and accommodations, plus she's not a prisoner here and permitted to leave the palace to walk the streets with or without an escort — Hethia cuts you off with a sharp downward gesture of her hand. "Given that boer'alvar of the druidic persuasion are meant to at least appear ascetic, this could easily have been taken as an insult by the less forgiving. Like I said, several of my own people are itching for an excuse, any excuse to take offense at the var Ridell line and smear the peace effort. She needs to shape up, and fast — rulership is hard, brutal, and unforgiving." So... why doesn't she tell Ryn that? Right now Ryn has scant few allies as regent — by your reckoning, Elthara may be the only one who's genuinely out to help Ryn with this whole rulership thing. If she has insights, maybe she should share them, if she has problems with how she's being treated here in the palace, maybe she should say something. Ryn's getting a crash course in regency and she needs all the help she can get. "Hmph. Well, maybe I'll do that." If she doesn't mind. You just want to help Ryn here, and she doesn't have to like you to see the benefit in endearing herself to the primary negotiator on the opposing side. "So, that would be Elthara? As things stand, the regent may as well be a puppet." You sigh. This is going to take some time. |"It's painful to walk these halls, see how much has changed in the scant space of two and a half centuries. Everything has been so smoothly and efficiently removed, or converted to the worship of this sun goddess from the south. How swift they were to banish all imagery of the Old Wyld from the carvings and murals that once honored it, or turned them to depict reverence of this Lumia." You're not really surprised at that. History's borne out that when one faction takes over from another, the first thing that's done is to get rid of all of the symbols of the old regime; it's nothing new or particular to the pale elves. A sigh. "I know, I know. Atheldred var Ridell was a woman who didn't flinch from doing what she believed to be right and necessary, and that was what made her absolutely and brutally efficient and terrifying. Maybe that's why Vaeril Xadaron didn't fight her over the conversion of the boer'alvar and chose to exile himself and his instead. "But even so... the chapel to Lumia used to be a shrine to the Old Wyld, complete with a planted bough from a wyld tree. I was told stories of the yearly ceremonies that were open to the public, and felt proud to be an initiate in a druidic circle, even as a child... I know that even the wyld trees have said their time has passed, but the sight of these changes still evokes emotions that can't be denied." It's then that Hethia catches herself, realizing that she's said too much and she's supposed to be standoffish with you. Seeing her clam up like that is an experience; the instantaneous transformation back to snobbish, cold and haughty elf is the quickest about-face you've seen. "Well, it doesn't matter now. The battle's lost, and we're discussing the terms of surrender. What good does getting sentimental do?" The good it's doing here is that you've gotten to understand her a little better, and hopefully the same can be said in reverse. That's important if everyone's going to walk out of this with an agreement that's tolerable to all parties involved. |"Perhaps the thing that annoys me most about all of this is the way wargs are made to wear those ridiculous animal clothes while in the palace — " Hethia says with a snort, folding her arms. "Completely and utterly impractical for any animal who intends to do useful work or retain her dignity — while being marked as little more than a toy dog at the same time. They didn't use to do that before the schism, so I'm told — and now poor Norathar has to bear that indignity for my sake." You don't know about that — it can look pretty good on them. That, and you understand that other peoples put barding on their combat mounts to protect them; this presumably isn't any different. Hethia sniffs. "Of course, I wouldn't expect you to know. Wargs don't need armor — they are not made to take blows like a horse might be able to, but instead evade them, and armor would only slow them down and get in their way. My dear Norathar is a lovely, graceful creature, not some lump of muscle and meat." You think otherwise, but telling Hethia that wouldn't be constructive, as satisfying as it would be. Well, when in Belhar, do as the Belharans do, and dog armor is part and parcel of the accepted etiquette here. "Hmph. The sacrifices we all make for peace." | |"It's a change of pace in lifestyle. Certainly far cushier than what I'm used to — I've maintained my ascetic lifestyle as best as I can, but I still do not wish to tarry overlong within these walls. They make you grow weak." Ascetic, huh. Well, the idea that most people get when they hear the word "druid" is sleeping on roots and under boughs, frolicking about naked, that kind of thing. Hethia scowls. "It's the wyld elves that started all that nonsense centuries ago, and no one's really ever tried to make the distinction between us and our cousins. [silly |Damned hippies, I tell you — they just need to get haircuts and jobs already. ]But no, [pc.name] — we used to have some fairly grand temples and arboretums out there in the Frostwood, all of them built in the same style, even if smaller in scale than this palace and with a lot more greenery." And then the Godswar happened, you take it. "In a sense, but not in the way you probably imagine. The wraiths didn't attack us directly, and instead sent their servants to spread a fungal blight that struck at the wyld trees. Through our link with them, we were afflicted too, and that's how we became a nonentity in the conflict — our druidic magics were worthless against the blight specifically tailored to turn our powers against us." And that opened the door for people to turn to Lumia for salvation. Hethia swallows hard. "Yes." So the temples still stand? "A few. Too many of us died — especially the archdruid of the time, Vaeril Xadaron — and we didn't have the hands to maintain them in the state they ought to be. After the schism, the funding from the Winter Palace that was meant for the upkeep of the temples dried up like thin spit on a hot stove, going to the worship of Lumia instead. Furthermore, many sites were voluntarily abandoned — many of the survivors didn't want to linger in places that held bad memories for them. Only one or two still remain in actual use, and in a far reduced capacity." And it's only been two and a half centuries — barely a generation or two. A sigh. "Time seems to go by so quickly these days. We have to keep up with the other races even if it means feeling rushed all the time, don't we? But yes, even if my previous accommodations were more ascetic that all this grandeur, I'm no stranger to sleeping in beds, [pc.name]. You don't have to worry about that." |"Ever since I've been a guest of the Regent's, I've taken to studying the palace itself, seeing just how far it's fallen from the stories of the glory it used to hold." Oh? You'd say it's pretty impressive and glorious as it is right now. Of course, if that simply meant it was more so in the past... "It was. We have depictions of the palace on murals in our temples; we wanted to keep the histories as accurate as possible so we could properly track the decline of the Winter City without the light of druidic guidance. How ironic that we fell before they did..." You have your own doubts about them actually keeping an accurate picture of the situation instead of the narrative they wanted to push, but at least Hethia's being quite blatant about it without outright saying it out loud. ] |[rand |"It's a change of pace in lifestyle. Certainly not what I've grown used to out in the Frostwood in form, but the function isn't too far off." Yeah, the idea that most people get when they hear the word "druid" is sleeping on roots and under boughs, frolicking about naked, that kind of thing. Hethia sighs. "It's the wyld elves that started all that nonsense millennia ago, and no one's really ever tried to make the distinction between us and our cousins. [silly |Damned hippies, I tell you — they just need to get haircuts and jobs already. ]But no, [pc.name] — we used to have some fairly grand temples and arboretums out there in the Frostwood, all of them built in the same style, even if smaller in scale than this palace and with a lot more greenery." And then the Godswar happened, you take it. "In a sense, but not in the way you probably imagine. The wraiths didn't attack us directly, and instead sent their servants to spread a fungal blight that struck at the wyld trees. Through our link with them, we were afflicted too, and that's how we became a nonentity in the conflict — our druidic magics were worthless against the blight specifically tailored to turn our powers against us." And that opened the door for people to turn to Lumia for salvation. Hethia swallows hard. "Yes." So the temples still stand? "A few. Too many of us died — especially the archdruid of the time, Vaeril Xadaron — and we didn't have the hands to maintain them in the state they ought to be. After the schism, the funding from the Winter Palace that was meant for the upkeep of the temples dried up like thin spit on a hot stove, going to the worship of Lumia instead. Furthermore, many sites were voluntarily abandoned — many of the survivors didn't want to linger in places that held bad memories for them. Only one or two still remain in actual use, and in a far reduced capacity." And it's only been two and a half centuries — barely a generation or two. A sigh. "Time seems to go by so quickly these days. We have to keep up with the other races even if it means feeling rushed all the time, don't we? But yes, even if my previous accommodations were more ascetic that all this grandeur, I'm no stranger to sleeping in beds, [pc.name]. You don't have to worry about that." |"The Regent has been very kind and made sure I've wanted for nothing during my stay. Within reason, of course." Makes sense. This is the first major test of Ryn's reign, and she doesn't want to risk messing it up in the slightest. "Her intentions are good, but it's clear that her inexperience shows. I cannot really blame her for assuming that I'd want, say, lavish meals and quarters as a matter of course as opposed to a more ascetic way of living while a guest in her palace, but others may not be so forgiving and far quicker to judge her for imagined slights, especially when they want to find fault with her." She's doing very well for someone who was in her circumstances. Alissa clearly had no intention of ever letting the so-called Duchess of the Rim hold any kind of genuine responsibility, authority or influence, and so Ryn's schooling in rulership was nonexistent. Right now, Elthara and Hethia herself are the only people whom she can truly trust while the Winter City gets back on its feet. "I won't deny that there've been some calls from druidic hardliners to push for a more demanding stance at the negotiations; even now, they cling to the faint hope that they can turn the boer'alvar back to the Old Wyld, even when the wyld trees themselves have accepted their passing. It is true that I'm here to try and obtain a favorable outcome for the schismatics... but trying to screw over someone who's only been reasonable with me is something I'm not on board with." Those druids sure sound vindictive. "Oh trust me, there're those in Elthara's circles who think the same way, only directed against us; one shouldn't be surprised if the only thing the regent means to them is an avenue through which to get what they want. Politics as usual." [pc.bg noblescion |Oh, you know about all of that. Even if you were the spare of a spare and had no chance of ever participating in such politicking despite being nobility, you'd seen enough of that in your youth to know you wanted no part of it; you'd rather have wrestled wild beasts. |Well, good thing that you never had the opportunity to get close to any of that nastiness, let alone participate in it. Sounds like horrible business. ] "It is. Frankly, I think the regent is in less danger when she's out with you hunting her sister than here in what's ostensibly her own home." Ah... how true. Ryn needs friends more than ever, and you're counting on both Hethia and Elthara to keep the wolves at bay while you're out there. |"I suppose my biggest complaint is that wargs, be they riding or otherwise, have to be clothed in barding when they're out of their stables in the city. That wasn't a custom before the schism — I suppose it's an easy way to distinguish our wargs from their wargs." You've seen the silvered barding that her warg wears, as with some of the other beasts prowling the palace with their guard handlers. It's very pretty, but also looks to be more ceremonial than anything else. "It vexes Norathar to no end — very constraining, and she can't wait for the end of the day for us to return so she can take it off. But we all make sacrifices for peace, and even she has to admit that discomfort is a small price to pay for our success. When in the palace, do as the snobs do, I suppose. They didn't even have one tailored for her — it was a hand-me-down from another bitch to be provided on short notice, and she complains about the lingering scent all day." Hah... "If that's the greatest of my complaints — or at least, those that don't come as part and parcel of my task — I guess I've got it pretty good. Plus, Norathar acknowledges that her discomfort isn't much compared to what I have to do day in, day out — she's such a sanguine pup." |"Yesterday, I took several of the other druids out to the city at large — under guard, of course — to see what had become of the Winter City in their absence. Most of them agree that they don't want to live in the city walls proper even after re-integration; there's talk of outlying settlements within reach of the city proper. Close enough to be available, far enough to not place undue strain on the Winter City's infrastructure." That doesn't bode very well for re-integration of them, though, not to mention the reunification of the pale elves as a people. Still, it's a step forward. "Even before the schism, we were a bit removed from boer'alvar society — the temples to the Old Wyld were where druids would mingle with the people at large. Now that they've been repurposed as temples to this Lumia goddess — " her face crumples up into a scowl — "there's even less reason for us to have an established presence in the Winter City. The people seem happy worshipping Lumia... happier than they were under the old scheme of things." That's... that's very honest of her to be able to admit as much. That realization must have been a bitter pill to swallow. "It was, but it's the truth. The wyld trees were right — we can't really compete with the likes of that. There's no way we can provoke some kind of revival in the people of the Winter City — they can't go back, not after we failed them so deeply. The others will call this defeatist talk, but we have to move on. It was a while before I realized this for myself, walking down the streets of the Winter City... hopefully they'll come around to it on their own as well." |"To be honest, I don't know how to feel about staying here. Legend has it that the Old Wyld aided in the making of the palace, carving the palace both out of and into the glacier; when that was done, boer'alvar hands smoothed the floors and walls and put the touch of civilization over the foundation of nature." She sighs and sweeps a hand over the corridor with its columns and frescoes. "But looking at it now, it doesn't look like something that we would have created. I spent all my life amongst the old temples hidden deep within the Frostwood, and... it's just fundamentally different in a way that I can't quite put into words." Hm... "Were we the ones that changed during our exile in the woods? Were the adherents of the human goddess the ones to transform the palace so completely and utterly? Or did the change begin even before the Godswar? I don't know — just staying here's raised so many questions that I'd never taken the time to consider before. I wonder if Elthara would think the same way if she were to visit us for a spell." That remains to be seen. On one hand, Elthara's hard-headed. On the other hand, Hethia's living proof that hard-headedness doesn't necessarily mean being unable to change one's views in light of new evidence and perspectives. You'll have to see how things shake out, but it isn't a lost cause. ] ]
rows.translation: [hethia.isHostile |[rand |哼，这样已经足够了。摄政王本人倒是挺通情达理的，但很明显，她在外交事务方面确实没什么经验——否则她就不会按照自己的标准而不是代表们的标准来挑选使者了。当然，也不指望她能懂这些，但其他人可不会像她这样体谅别人的。 我 每当他们想找她的茬时，总是会因为一些鸡毛蒜皮的小事来指责她。” “怎么了？你应该明白，赫希娅已经得到了冰之宫殿所能提供的最好待遇。有食宿，而且她在这里并不是囚犯，可以自由离开宫殿，无论是否有人陪同都可以在街上行走——” 赫希娅突然用手势打断了你：“既然那些信奉德鲁伊教的布尔人至少应该 出现 对于那些心胸狭隘的人来说，这种言辞很容易被理解为一种侮辱。正如我所说，我的团队中就有几个人一直在寻找借口，任何借口都可以让他们借机对Var Ridell的立场表示不满，进而破坏当前的和平努力。 她必须尽快做出改变——统治事业充满艰辛、残酷，而且容不得半点懈怠。 那么……她为什么不把这一点告诉瑞恩呢？目前，作为摄政王，瑞恩几乎没有什么盟友；按照你的说法，艾尔塔拉可能是唯一真正愿意帮助瑞恩应对这些统治挑战的人了。 如果她有什么见解，或许应该分享出来；如果她对宫廷里对待她的方式感到不满，或许也应该说出来。瑞恩正在快速学习关于摄政的相关知识，她需要一切可能的帮助。 哼，好吧，也许我会这么做的。” 只要她不介意的话。你只是想帮助Ryn而已，她并不一定要喜欢你，才能明白讨好对方的主要谈判者对自己来说有什么好处。 所以，那就是艾尔塔拉吗？就目前的情况来看，那位摄政王其实不过是个傀儡罢了。” 你叹了口气。这件事看来需要一些时间才能解决。 |走在这些走廊里，看着短短两个半世纪里发生的一切变化，真的让人感到痛心。一切都发生得如此悄无声息，却又如此彻底。 高效地 这些象征被移除，或者被改造成用来崇拜这位来自南方的太阳女神。他们是多么迅速地将那些曾经用来纪念古老荒野的所有图像从雕刻和壁画上清除掉，或者将它们改造成用来表达对这位卢米娅的崇敬之情。 对此，你其实并不感到惊讶。历史已经证明，当一个派系取代另一个派系时，他们首先会做的就是消除旧政权的所有象征；这对于苍白精灵来说，并不是什么新鲜事，也不是什么特别的现象。 一声叹息。“我知道，我知道。阿瑟尔德雷德·瓦·里德尔是一个从不畏惧去做自己认为正确且必要的事情的女性，正是这一点使她变得极其高效、冷酷无情，同时也令人胆寒。也许正因为如此，瓦雷尔·扎达隆才没有因为她对‘博尔阿尔瓦’的改造计划而与她抗争，而是选择自我流放，带着他的族人一起离开了。 但即便如此……卢米娅的小教堂曾经是古老荒野的神圣之地，那里甚至种着一棵来自荒野的树木。人们告诉我，那里每年都会举行向公众开放的仪式，即使还是个孩子，我也为自己能够成为德鲁伊团体的成员而感到自豪……我知道，就连那些荒野之树也早已宣告它们的时代已经结束，但看到这些变化，我依然会感受到一些无法抑制的情感。 就在这时，赫希娅才回过神来，意识到自己说得太多了——她本来应该对你保持疏离的态度的。看到她突然变得沉默寡言，真是令人印象深刻；她那瞬间变回傲慢、冷漠、高傲的精灵形象，绝对是你见过的最迅速的“转变”了。 嗯，现在这些都无所谓了。战斗已经失败，我们正在讨论投降的条件。在这种情况下，感伤有什么用呢？” 不过，在这种情况下，感伤反而能让你更好地理解她，而希望她也能同样理解你。如果大家都能达成让所有相关方都能接受的协议，那么这一点就非常重要了。 |或许所有这些事情中最让我恼火的就是，那些狼人在宫殿里非得穿着那些荒谬的动物服装——”赫希娅哼了一声，双臂交叉说道，“对于任何想要从事实际工作或保持自己尊严的动物来说，这种服装都完全不实用；同时，它们也因此被贬低为不过是玩具狗罢了。 据我所知，在分裂之前他们并不习惯这样做——而现在，可怜的诺拉塔尔却不得不因为我的缘故承受这种羞辱。 你可能不知道，这种装饰对他们来说反而会显得很漂亮。而且，你也明白，其他人会在他们的战斗坐骑上安装护甲来保护它们；想必这种做法也没有什么不同吧。 赫希娅哼了一声：“当然，我也没指望你会知道。狼人本来就不会 需要 盔甲并不是为了像马那样承受冲击而设计的，它的作用其实是帮助角色躲避攻击；相反，盔甲只会减慢行动速度，妨碍行动。我亲爱的诺拉瑟尔，是一只可爱而优雅的生物，而不是仅仅由肌肉和肉块构成的。你可能有不同的看法，但告诉赫希娅这些并没有什么意义，尽管这样做会让你感到满足。嗯，在贝尔哈尔，就应该按照贝尔哈尔人的方式来行事，而狗皮护甲正是这里人们所接受的礼仪规范的一部分。 哼，我们所有人为和平所做出的牺牲啊。 | |这是一种生活方式上的改变。当然，这里比我习惯的环境要舒适得多——我一直在尽力保持自己那种苦行僧般的生活方式，但我还是不想在这些墙壁里待得太久。这样的环境会让人变得软弱。苦行僧啊……嗯，大多数人听到‘德鲁伊’这个词时，想到的应该是在树根旁或树枝下睡觉、光着身子嬉戏之类的形象吧。” 赫希娅皱起了眉头。 几个世纪前，正是那些野精灵挑起了这一切麻烦事，而且从来没有人真正尝试过区分我们和我们的那些‘表亲’。 [silly |该死的嬉皮士们，我跟你们说——他们根本就应该去剪剪头发，找份工作才对。 ]但是，并非如此。 [pc.name] 在霜林里，我们曾经建造过一些规模相当宏大的寺庙和植物园，它们的建筑风格都是一样的。虽然那些建筑规模比这座宫殿要小，而且周围也种植了更多的绿植。” 然后，神战就发生了，你懂的。 从某种意义上来说，但并不是你想象中的那种方式。那些幽灵并没有直接攻击我们，而是派出了它们的仆从来传播一种真菌疫病，这种疫病专门针对那些野生树木。由于我们与它们存在着某种联系，我们也受到了影响，因此我们在这场冲突中变得毫无作用——我们的德鲁伊魔法对这种专门用来削弱我们力量的疫病来说，根本毫无效果。 而这为人们寻求卢米亚的帮助打开了大门。 赫希娅艰难地咽了口唾沫：“是的。” 那么那些神庙现在还存在着吗？ “还有几座。但是太多人失去了生命——尤其是当时的大德鲁伊瓦埃里尔·萨达隆——我们已经没有足够的人力来维护那些神庙，让它们保持应有的状态了。 分裂发生后，原本用于维护这些寺庙的冬宫资金就像热锅上的薄痰一样迅速枯竭，这些资金反而被用来祭祀卢米娅了。此外，许多遗址也被人们主动放弃了——许多幸存者并不愿意继续留在那些让他们充满痛苦回忆的地方。 实际上，现在只有一两种还在被使用，而且其使用规模也已经大大缩减了。 才仅仅两个半世纪而已——几乎还不到一两代人的时间。
